title: Proposing GRENDEL: GalleRy ExperimeNt for Decays of Exotic LLPs at the LHC
summary: Long-lived particles are a generic prediction of Standard Model extensions that address the hierarchy problem, the origin of neutrino masses, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, and the nature of dark matter. Despite the breadth of theoretical motivation, neutral long-lived particles in the GeV-scale mass range remain difficult to probe at the LHC main detectors, where trigger limitations and challenging backgrounds curtail sensitivity over a wide range of lifetimes. We propose GRENDEL (GalleRy ExperimeNt for Decays of Exotic LLPs), a dedicated detector to be installed in the PX56 drainage gallery at CMS Point 5. GRENDEL will exploit the substantial rock and concrete between the detector and LHC interaction point as passive shielding in addition to employing active background rejection. Located approximately 22 m above the interaction point and running largely transverse to the beam, GRENDEL will span around 110 m and cover the central region $|η| < 0.6$. GRENDEL will make use of extruded scintillator bars to achieve competitive sensitivity with other proposed detectors while requiring minimal infrastructure, and without the need for civil engineering. We present the physics case, detector concept, and projected sensitivities to heavy neutral leptons, dark scalars, and axion-like particles covering the $0.2-15$ GeV mass range with 3 $\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ of HL-LHC data. The benchmarks span the neutrino, scalar, and axion portals, with production through exotic Higgs decays, $B$- and $D$-meson decays, and $W/Z$ decays.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes GRENDEL, a new detector designed to identify long-lived particles in the GeV mass range at the LHC, overcoming challenges related to current detection methods.
AI.motivation: To address fundamental problems in particle physics, such as the hierarchy problem, neutrino masses, baryon asymmetry, and dark matter, which may involve long-lived neutral particles.
AI.method: GRENDEL is a dedicated detector utilizing passive shielding from the surrounding rock and concrete, alongside active background rejection, to enhance sensitivity in detecting long-lived particles with minimal infrastructure.
AI.result: With a projected sensitivity to various particles (heavy neutral leptons, dark scalars, axion-like particles) across a mass range of 0.2-15 GeV using data from the HL-LHC, GRENDEL aims to effectively probe areas previously challenging to explore.
AI.conclusion: GRENDEL represents a promising approach to discovering new physics through the detection of long-lived particles, leveraging a novel detector design and strategic location at the LHC.

title: Improved Threshold for Particle-Induced Magnetic Avalanche in Single-Molecule Magnets Using Fe$_8$ Molecule
summary: Extending the original work on the development of a magnetic avalanche detector using Mn$_{12}$-ac single-molecule magnet (SMM), we report the results on a significantly lower threshold magnetic avalanche detector using Fe$_8$ SMM. Fe$_8$ has an order of magnitude smaller relaxation time that is expected to produce at least 3 orders of magnitude lower avalanche threshold compared to Mn$_{12}$-ac. We confirm this experimentally through the detection of gamma particles with energy at least two orders of magnitude lower than the original Mn$_{12}$-ac detection demonstrated using alpha particles, limited by the experimentally available radiation source. The true threshold of avalanche may be significantly lower and will be explored with lower energy x-rays and potentially infrared photons.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a lower threshold magnetic avalanche detector using Fe$_8$ single-molecule magnet, achieving significantly enhanced sensitivity compared to the previously studied Mn$_{12}$-ac.
AI.motivation: To improve the sensitivity and performance of magnetic avalanche detectors for particle detection.
AI.method: Utilizing Fe$_8$ single-molecule magnet to decrease the relaxation time and consequently the avalanche threshold for detecting gamma particles.
AI.result: Experimental detection of gamma particles at energies two orders of magnitude lower than those detected by Mn$_{12}$-ac, with expectations of even lower thresholds with different radiation types.
AI.conclusion: The Fe$_8$ SMM shows promising potential for further reducing detection thresholds, warranting future exploration with lower energy sources.

title: Panda Diplomacy: Foundation Model Pre-training across Particle Imaging Detectors for High Energy and Nuclear Physics
summary: Foundation models are increasingly being pursued in particle and nuclear physics, but existing approaches remain strongly tied to individual experiments through detector-specific architectures or pre-training objectives, limiting their reuse across sensing modalities. We show that a point cloud self-distillation framework yields a substantially more general sensor-level pre-training recipe. We show that the same refined architecture and objective can be independently pre-trained with minimal changes on three qualitatively different detector modalities: liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC), collider TPC, and water Cherenkov. Using 1,000 labeled images for downstream task adaptation, Panda V2 matches or exceeds specialized foundation-model baselines trained with orders of magnitude more supervision, matching state-of-the-art particle-clustering performance with 70x fewer labeled events on sPHENIX while substantially improving particle identification, and on LArTPC data matching Panda (arXiv:2512.01324) particle reconstruction with up to 1,000x fewer labels. Beyond reconstruction, simple linear probes reveal physically meaningful latent structure associated with particle causality and track curvature.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a generalized point cloud self-distillation framework for particle detection that allows for effective pre-training across different detector types with significantly fewer labeled images, achieving state-of-the-art results in particle identification and clustering.
AI.motivation: Existing foundation models in particle and nuclear physics are limited by their dependence on specific detector types, impeding broader application and reuse.
AI.method: The authors propose a point cloud self-distillation framework that allows for independent pre-training across three diverse detector modalities using the same architecture and objectives.
AI.result: Using only 1,000 labeled images for downstream tasks, the model, Panda V2, achieves or surpasses the performance of models that require substantially more labeled data, showcasing improved particle identification and clustering results.
AI.conclusion: The approach not only enhances reconstruction accuracy significantly due to lower labeling requirements but also reveals valuable latent structures related to particle behavior.

title: Neutrino Experiments at the LHC and the HL-LHC
summary: High energy neutrinos are copiously produced in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), located at CERN, near Geneva, Switzerland. In particular, a large neutrino flux is expected in the far-forward direction. This flux is concentrated near the beam axis, reaches energies up to the TeV scale, and for electron and tau neutrinos can be dominated by heavy flavour decays at the highest energies. These features open a new experimental window for studying neutrino interactions with dedicated forward detectors, in an energy range beyond the reach of traditional accelerator-based neutrino experiments. The new FASER and SND@LHC experiments reported the first direct observations of neutrino interactions at a hadron collider using the first data from Run 3, which started in 2022. Since then, the programme has advanced to the first measurements, including charged-current neutrino-nucleon cross sections and the detection of different neutrino flavours. This article describes the forward neutrino flux at the LHC, the acceptance and detector concepts of the Run 3 experiments, and summarises the current status of collider neutrino measurements. It also discusses prospects for extending this neutrino programme towards the HL-LHC era. The collected data will also provide constraints on very forward hadron production, and enable searches for feebly interacting particles.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses high energy neutrinos produced at the LHC, reports observations and measurements from new experiments, and outlines future prospects for neutrino research.
AI.motivation: Studying high energy neutrinos offers insight into interactions at energies beyond traditional experiments, leveraging the unique environment of the LHC.
AI.method: Analyzed neutrino flux in the far-forward direction, conducted measurements of neutrino interactions using FASER and SND@LHC detectors during Run 3 of the LHC.
AI.result: Achieved direct observations of neutrino interactions, measured charged-current neutrino-nucleon cross sections, and identified various neutrino flavours.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance understanding of collider neutrino measurements and set the stage for future investigations into feebly interacting particles and hadron production.

title: Reining in an Agentic Harness for High Energy Physics
comment: 13 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables; includes a glossary
summary: Agentic systems now address tasks across theoretical, phenomenological, and experimental high energy physics (HEP), but their scientific capabilities remain difficult to reuse across different large language models, providers, and harnesses. We argue that stable parts of these workflows should be promoted into versioned scientific operations and exposed through common protocols. Existing general-purpose harnesses can then be specialized for HEP through task-specific sets of tools and skills, while community-maintained registries would make these capabilities discoverable and citable. We identify mismatches in conventions, assumptions, and domains of validity among independently developed operations as a potential obstacle to their composition, and discuss machine-readable scientific contracts as one possible solution. These design principles and evaluation guidelines provide a near-term path toward a portable and community-maintained agentic harness for HEP.

AI.tldr: The paper advocates for enhancing reusability in high energy physics (HEP) workflows by promoting stable components into standardized operations using common protocols.
AI.motivation: To improve the scientific capabilities of agentic systems in HEP and facilitate their reuse across various platforms.
AI.method: Propose versioned scientific operations, common protocols, and machine-readable scientific contracts to address mismatches in independent operations.
AI.result: Identification of obstacles in current workflows and potential solutions that allow for better composition and specialization of tools in HEP.
AI.conclusion: The proposed design principles and guidelines lead towards a more portable, community-maintained agentic harness for high energy physics.

title: Isospectral potentials with Dirac delta interaction: Constrained Spectra
summary: We study quantum potentials containing Dirac delta function (DDF) within its supersymmetric (isospectral) construction via a discontinuous superpotential, instead of being simply an added part. This construction comprises of two independently solvable sectors joined at the singular point by matching conditions imposed by the corresponding self-adjoint extension. Needing careful regularization, these boundary conditions impose independent algebraic constraints on each of the eigenstates, that restrict and truncate the spectrum. The number of surviving bound states, which are required to be parity-even, is thus fixed by the available system parameters rather than by the usual quantization rule. The specific cases of the Harmonic oscillator and the Rosen-Morse potential isospectrally infused with the DDF demonstrate such highly restrictive spectra, while the similar combination of the DDF with a Calogero-type singularity turns out to be largely incompatible as the regularization breaks down. Therefore, localized singularities are capable of controlling and engineering the discrete spectrum of quantum systems, with possible use in myriads of physical systems with very localized interactions.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates how Dirac delta function potentials in quantum systems affect the spectral properties via supersymmetric constructions, showing that localized singularities can engineer discrete spectra.
AI.motivation: To explore the impact of Dirac delta function potentials on the spectra of quantum systems through a new supersymmetric approach.
AI.method: A discontinuous superpotential with matching conditions at singular points is used to create isospectral constructions that yield independently solvable sectors and regularized boundary conditions.
AI.result: The number of bound states is determined by system parameters instead of traditional quantization rules, showing highly restrictive spectra in specific potentials like the Harmonic oscillator and Rosen-Morse potential, while revealing incompatibility with Calogero-type singularities.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that localized singularities can effectively engineer quantum spectra, suggesting potential applications in systems with localized interactions.

title: Causal self-consistency of the Blandford--McKee self-similar solution
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, submitted to Physics of Fluids
summary: The Blandford--McKee (BM) solution describes the ultra-relativistic self-similar flow behind a strong spherical blast wave propagating into an external density profile $\propto r^{-k}$, where $k<4$ and $r$ is the distance from the center, but it applies only to the hot shell adjacent to the shock, sufficiently deep behind it, the fluid leaves the BM regime. Since the similarity profiles are determined solely by the shock conditions, with no conditions imposed at the inner end, the validity of the solution near the shock depends on whether the flow beyond the BM regime can imprint on this hot shell. For shallow density profiles, $k<k_g\simeq 2.062$, the characteristic structure of the BM solution already prevents forward-going acoustic information from the non-BM interior from reaching the shock during the ultra-relativistic stage. For steeper profiles, $k_g<k<4$, the hot equation of state fails while the flow is still relativistic and shock-connected. There, we derive a new self-similar solution for the cooling relativistic flow, which has its own similarity scale, equations, and characteristic structure. It overlaps with the hot BM solution toward the shock, and reaches a sonic point beyond this overlap. This critical point separates the shock-connected BM-plus-cooling composite from the deeper downstream region, so acoustic signals generated beyond it cannot propagate toward the shock. The mechanism is explicit at $k=7/2$, for which the cooling solution is obtained analytically. This causal structure is therefore what enables the BM solution, which remains self-consistent near the shock even though it does not globally describe the full downstream flow.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Blandford--McKee solution for ultra-relativistic flows behind spherical blast waves, revealing the limitations of the BM framework under varying density profiles and introducing a new solution for cooling relativistic flows.
AI.motivation: To understand the limitations of the BM solution in ultra-relativistic flows and how it can be extended to account for cooling effects in different density profiles.
AI.method: The authors derive a new self-similar solution for cooling relativistic flow, particularly for denser profiles with $k_g < k < 4$, establishing a critical sonic point that delineates different flow regimes.
AI.result: The new solution overlaps with the hot BM solution near the shock and distinguishes the nature of acoustic propagation in the flow, demonstrating that, for certain density profiles, acoustic signals cannot reach the shock.
AI.conclusion: The study illustrates that while the BM solution is valid near the shock, it does not encompass the entirety of the downstream flow, especially in the presence of cooling effects, with potential implications for understanding relativistic blast waves.

authors: Maurice H. P. M. van Putten
title: Efficient searches of small signals across two-channel noisy data: a challenge in Big Data observations
summary: Searching for novel small signals in noisy data is preferably pursued by correlation in two or more independently operating channels. Signals of potential interest exist in tails beyond $κσ$, where $κ$ denotes a multiple of the standard deviation $σ$ of the data. Since moving data is a major cost factor in Big Data analysis and heterogeneous computing more generally, efficiency may be optimized by restricting the correlations computation to the tails of two-channel data exceeding $κσ$. Already, a moderate value $κ\gtrsim2$ realizes a data-reduction by at least an order of magnitude. Here, we study this approach using a novel {\it Excess Probability Ratio} (EPR), correlating Boolean data resulting from tails beyond a cut-off $κσ$. We compare and rank EPR performance against conventional direct cross-correlation (DCC) and Pearson coefficient (PC), applicable to the original data with no cut-off. This benchmark is performed over different combinations of background noise Gaussian, Poisson and Uniform and signals Gaussian, Poisson, Uniform, Chirps and Sine waves. Results show performance of EPR to be comparable to that of PC, providing a new approach for significant improvements in efficiency with essentially no loss of sensitivity, relevant to the present era of Big Data observatories.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a novel method for efficiently correlating signals in noisy data by focusing on extremes in the data distribution, specifically using the Excess Probability Ratio (EPR) to improve data analysis in Big Data contexts without sacrificing sensitivity.
AI.motivation: The study aims to optimize efficiency in Big Data analysis by reducing the computational burden associated with moving large datasets, particularly by focusing on signal tails that exceed a certain threshold defined by the product of standard deviation.
AI.method: The authors introduce the Excess Probability Ratio (EPR) which computes correlations only in the tails of data distributions, specifically for data exceeding a cut-off defined by κσ, comparing its performance against direct cross-correlation (DCC) and the Pearson coefficient (PC).
AI.result: EPR shows comparable performance to the Pearson coefficient while enabling a substantial data reduction, with reductions by at least an order of magnitude when κ is set to values around 2.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides significant efficiency improvements in processing noisy data within Big Data observatories, maintaining high sensitivity despite the data cut-off.

title: Time performance of USTC-IME LGAD under synchrotron light source focused X-ray
summary: The time performance of Low Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs), designed by the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and fabricated by the Institute of Microelectronics of Chinese Academy of Sciences (IME), was characterized at the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF). The experiment was conducted at the BL16B1 beamline, which delivers a focused X-ray beam with a diameter of 500 μm, a repetition period of 2 ns, and a photon energy of 10 keV. Using a fast oscilloscope, waveforms containing continuous signal pulses were recorded within a 50 ns time window. The LGAD under test successfully resolved the 2 ns period of the SSRF. To mitigate pile-up effects and extract pulse-by-pulse information from the acquired waveforms, a waveform-level global template fitting method was employed. The time resolution was then estimated using a combined profile likelihood approach, yielding a value of 126.6 ps. The effect of random photon absorption depth on the time resolution of LGADs was studied through dedicated simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the time performance of LGADs, revealing a time resolution of 126.6 ps using a global template fitting method.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the performance of LGADs in time-resolved applications, ensuring precise measurements are achievable in experimental setups.
AI.method: Characterization of LGADs using a focused X-ray beam, recording waveforms with a fast oscilloscope and applying waveform-level global template fitting for data analysis.
AI.result: Achieved a time resolution of 126.6 ps, effectively resolving a 2 ns period, while addressing pile-up effects in waveform data.
AI.conclusion: The study enhances understanding of LGAD performance in photon timing applications and the impact of photon absorption depth on time resolution.

title: Validating a BDT-based Electron-Positron Identification Algorithm at CLAS12 with Experimental Data
summary: This article presents a machine-learning, particle-identification algorithm for electrons and positrons in the CLAS12 experiment. The main objective was to minimize charged-pion contamination for both experimental and simulated data. We developed, evaluated and validated two BDT models with different input features, both trained on simulated samples, and conducted rigorous validation using both simulated and experimental data to ensure reliability. Our results show the effectiveness of the applied models in mitigating background contamination. By retaining more than 90\% of leptons in the simulated samples, the charged-pion background is largely reduced. Performance was evaluated on experimental data, providing a framework to validate such approaches at CLAS12 and future electron-beam facilities.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a machine-learning algorithm for particle identification in the CLAS12 experiment, focusing on reducing charged-pion contamination and validating the effectiveness of two BDT models.
AI.motivation: The need to improve particle identification by minimizing background contamination from charged pions in experiments involving electrons and positrons.
AI.method: Two Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) models were developed and validated using both simulated and experimental data to assess their effectiveness in distinguishing leptons from charged pions.
AI.result: The models effectively retained over 90% of leptons in simulated data while significantly reducing the charged-pion background contamination.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide a validated framework for enhancing particle identification in CLAS12 and inform future developments in electron-beam facilities.

title: Solar Spin-Dependent Dark Matter-Neutron Cross Section Constraints: The Lost Case
summary: The Sun has long served as a natural dark matter detector, capturing halo particles that scatter with solar nuclei and electrons and subsequently produce indirect signals from dark matter annihilation that can be probed by either neutrino or $γ$-ray instruments. Previous efforts have computed cross-section constraints for dark matter scattering with electrons, as well as spin-independent and spin-dependent dark matter-proton scattering. However, the spin-dependent dark matter-neutron scattering scenario has been neglected, despite its importance in direct detection. For the first time, we compute the capture and evaporation rates for spin-dependent dark matter-neutron scattering in the Sun, including odd-neutron isotope targets in the current standard solar model. Comparing the predicted annihilation signals against current neutrino and $γ$-ray observations, and projecting the reach of upcoming detectors, we find that solar constraints exceed direct detection limits for several annihilation channels. For models in which the dark matter annihilates into long-lived mediators, these constraints can extend below the neutrino fog.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes spin-dependent dark matter-neutron scattering in the Sun, revealing that solar constraints on dark matter interactions surpass direct detection limits for certain annihilation channels.
AI.motivation: To investigate the neglected spin-dependent dark matter-neutron scattering scenario in the context of solar captures and its implications for indirect dark matter detection.
AI.method: Computed the capture and evaporation rates for spin-dependent dark matter-neutron scattering in the Sun using odd-neutron isotope targets and compared predicted annihilation signals with current observations and projections from upcoming detectors.
AI.result: Discovered that the resulting solar constraints exceed direct detection limits for several annihilation channels, particularly in models with long-lived mediators.
AI.conclusion: The study indicates that solar measurements can provide more restrictive limits on dark matter properties than previously understood, enhancing detection strategies.

title: Encoding Compact U(1) Gauge Fields in Bosonic Modes with GKP Stabilization
comment: 59 pages (32 main text + 20 appendices), 10 figures, 3 tables
summary: Compact lattice gauge theories are formulated in terms of angular variables and integer electric fluxes, while bosonic quantum hardware provides oscillator modes with continuous, unbounded quadratures. We bridge this gap with a one-to-one encoding. After Gauss's law is solved, each remaining gauge degree of freedom is carried by a single oscillator mode, with its interactions built from trigonometric gates, and a Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP)-type stabilizer provides the compactness that the hardware does not. The encoding becomes exact in the limit of infinite squeezing, and at finite squeezing, the leading imperfections act as small, computable shifts of physical observables rather than uncontrolled leakage. We apply the construction to compact QED$_3$ and derive the error budget at finite squeezing, characterizing the leading errors in closed form, and showing that they can be corrected, subtracted, or extrapolated away. We construct syndrome-extraction protocols that detect and remove the displacement component of photon loss, delimit the noise it does not reach, compare two choices of dynamical variables, and collect the scaling of mode count, gate count, and measurement cost. A one-plaquette example reproduces the exact compact-rotor dynamics, and real-time spectroscopy with controlled extrapolations recovers the exponentially small energy splitting between charge sectors, the seed of the monopole physics of the theory, at the percent level against its exact value.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the integration of compact lattice gauge theories with bosonic quantum hardware through a novel encoding method, demonstrating effective error correction and real-time spectroscopy techniques.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the discrete nature of compact lattice gauge theories with the continuous variables provided by bosonic quantum hardware.
AI.method: A one-to-one encoding is developed that associates gauge degrees of freedom with oscillator modes, utilizing trigonometric gates and stabilizers, while solving Gauss's law. The framework includes error analysis at finite squeezing and syndrome-extraction protocols for error mitigation.
AI.result: The approach allows for exact representation in the infinite squeezing limit and characterizes leading errors at finite squeezing, showing they are manageable. Additionally, a one-plaquette model simulates exact compact-rotor dynamics, and real-time spectroscopy achieves high precision in energy measurements related to monopole physics.
AI.conclusion: This framework effectively connects lattice gauge theories with quantum hardware, enabling advanced error correction and precise measurements, thereby advancing the study of monopole physics.

title: Redshift Identifiability from Gamma-Ray Burst Prompt Emission
summary: We examine which prompt-emission observables of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) carry identifiable redshift information in realistic structured-jet scenarios. By examining the photon-level Lorentz and cosmological transformations, we demonstrate any spectral observable reflecting the dominant-patch emission and any temporal observable reflecting the co-moving frame physics in the jet suffers from the same $z$-$θ_v$ degeneracy. The observable reflecting the absolute flux or count rate will also suffer from this $z$-$θ_v$ degeneracy in a different form. Due to the large variation of the intrinsic luminosity, combining the observables in the above-mentioned three classes cannot break this degeneracy. However, we demonstrate that two other classes of observables contain the potential to break this degeneracy: (i)~central engine-imprinted time scales, (ii)~emission from out of the dominant patch.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes gamma-ray burst prompt-emission observables for their redshift information, revealing that certain observable degeneracies exist, but proposes two new classes of observables that can potentially overcome these issues.
AI.motivation: To identify which gamma-ray burst observables can provide clear redshift information despite inherent degeneracies in existing metrics.
AI.method: The authors use photon-level Lorentz and cosmological transformations to examine various observables and their susceptibility to $z$-$θ_v$ degeneracies.
AI.result: Findings indicate that traditional observables are subject to the same degeneracies, but highlight two classes of observables with the potential to break these degeneracies.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the proposed new classes of observables could provide clearer insights into redshift information in structured jet scenarios.

title: Lynx2030 Science Analysis Group: Final Report
comment: White paper based on the Final Report by NASA's Lynx2030 Science Analysis Group
summary: The Lynx2030 Science Analysis Group (SAG) was convened to reassess the scientific goals and technical drivers of the Lynx mission concept amid a rapidly evolving astrophysics landscape. Building on the original Lynx Concept Study, the SAG examined how recent discoveries, emerging facilities, and advances in instrumentation influence the scientific opportunities for a next-generation flagship X-ray observatory. Through focused working groups, the SAG investigated the scientific impact of enhanced capabilities: (i) improved angular resolution, (ii) broader bandpass coverage, (iii) an enhanced microcalorimeter, (iv) new capabilities and observing modes, and (v) larger fields of view. Across a broad range of topics, from the formation of the first black holes and the evolution of galaxies to the baryon cycle, compact objects, stellar explosions, multi-messenger astrophysics, and the dynamic high-energy Universe, the SAG finds that the scientific motivation for a Lynx-class observatory remains compelling and, in many areas, has significantly strengthened over the past decade, prominently through JWST's discovery of the "Little Red Dots", likely massive accreting black holes in infant galaxies whose nature is fundamentally an X-ray question. This report shows that modest extensions beyond the original Lynx design reference mission can unlock transformative science while preserving the observatory's core architecture. Powerful current and future facilities such as Roman, Rubin, JWST, SKA, ngVLA, LISA, and NewAthena highlight the unique role a high-angular-resolution, high-throughput X-ray observatory would play in the multi-wavelength and multi-messenger ecosystem of the 2030s and beyond. The findings of the Lynx2030 SAG confirm Lynx's central vision: an unprecedented view of the hot and energetic Universe, enabling discoveries that will define high-energy astrophysics in the coming decades.

AI.tldr: The Lynx2030 SAG reassesses the Lynx mission's scientific goals in light of recent astrophysical advancements, confirming its relevance for future high-energy research.
AI.motivation: To adapt the Lynx mission concept to evolving astrophysical discoveries and emerging technologies in instrumentation.
AI.method: The SAG conducted focused group work to evaluate the impact of enhanced observatory capabilities on various astrophysical topics.
AI.result: The findings suggest significant advancements in understanding key astrophysical phenomena, particularly through discoveries made by JWST, notably related to accreting black holes.
AI.conclusion: Modest design modifications can greatly enhance the Lynx observatory's scientific potential, affirming its critical role in future astrophysical research.

title: Helium-Gas-Cooled Cryogenic Current Comparator Integrated with a Quantum Resistance Standard
summary: We report a cryogen-free cryogenic current comparator (CCC) system for precision resistance measurements. A helium-gas chamber was developed and installed on the 4 K stage of a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator equipped with a pulse-tube cryocooler. The CCC probe was housed in this chamber and was cooled through helium gas serving as a heat exchange medium. The metrological performance of this helium-gas-cooled CCC was evaluated through precision resistance-ratio measurements and found to be comparable to that obtained under liquid-helium cooling. A quantum Hall resistance (QHR) device was also integrated into the same refrigerator, enabling QHR/100~$Ω$ resistance-ratio measurements. The type-A uncertainty reached the 1~n$Ω$/$Ω$ level within an averaging time of 100~s, and the resulting resistance-ratio measurements agreed well with conventional liquid-helium-based measurements at the level of a few n$Ω$/$Ω$. The system provides this level of measurement performance while consuming less than 1~L of helium gas per thermal cycle.

AI.tldr: A cryogen-free system for precision resistance measurements was developed, utilizing a helium-gas chamber and tested for performance, showing results comparable to traditional liquid-helium systems.
AI.motivation: To develop a cryogen-free cryogenic current comparator system for more efficient and sustainable precision resistance measurements.
AI.method: A helium-gas chamber was installed on a dilution refrigerator, cooling a CCC probe, with evaluations through precision resistance-ratio measurements and integration of QHR for resistance measurements.
AI.result: The helium-gas-cooled CCC demonstrated metrological performance similar to liquid-helium cooling, achieving a type-A uncertainty of 1 n$Ω$/$Ω$ in 100 s and agreement with conventional measurements within a few n$Ω$/$Ω$.
AI.conclusion: This system offers high measurement precision while significantly reducing helium gas consumption, marking a step forward in cryogenic measurement technology.

title: Constraint on the Higgs boson width in the diphoton final state using signal-background interference in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to Physical Review Letters. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/HIG-25-004 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: The standard model Higgs boson, with a mass of 125 GeV, has a predicted decay width, $Γ_\mathrm{H}$, of 4.1 MeV. This Letter presents the first constraint on $Γ_\mathrm{H}$ obtained through the interference between the resonant H $\to$ $γγ$ process and the continuum $γγ$ production, both produced via gluon-gluon fusion. The analysis is performed using proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, collected by the CMS experiment between 2016 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. The observed (expected) limit on the Higgs boson width is $Γ_\mathrm{H}$ $\lt$ 92 (138) MeV at 95% confidence level. This is the most stringent constraint on $Γ_\mathrm{H}$ from on-shell Higgs boson measurements to date.

AI.tldr: The paper presents new constraints on the Higgs boson decay width from proton-proton collision data, marking the strongest limits established to date.
AI.motivation: To improve understanding of the Higgs boson properties and validate predictions from the standard model, particularly its decay width.
AI.method: Analysis of resonant H → γγ events and continuum γγ production using data from proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV and an integrated luminosity of 138 fb−1.
AI.result: The derived limits on the Higgs boson width are ΓH < 92 MeV observed and < 138 MeV expected at 95% confidence level.
AI.conclusion: This study provides the most stringent limits on the Higgs boson decay width from direct measurements, enhancing our knowledge of Higgs boson properties.

title: Neutrino Electroweak Couplings and the Neutrino Fog at Belle II
summary: The mono-photon process $e^+e^- \to γ+\mathrm{invisible}$ at Belle II probes both invisible new states and the electroweak couplings of neutrinos. In this work, we study the process $e^+e^- \to γν\barν$, finding that Belle II with the full expected dataset can determine the neutrino-sensitive effective weak mixing angle to a 3.6$\%$ relative statistical precision, competitive with existing neutrino probes at other energy scales. Polarized beams, as proposed for the Chiral Belle upgrade, separate the neutral- and charged-current contributions and provide independent access to each, giving a handle on the chiral structure of the neutrino gauge interactions. The same process is an irreducible background to dark boson searches, producing a neutrino fog once the luminosity exceeds 1 ab$^{-1}$.

AI.tldr: The study examines the $e^+e^- 	o γν arν$ process at Belle II, aiming to measure the effective weak mixing angle with high precision and investigate neutrino interactions using polarized beams.
AI.motivation: To explore the electroweak properties of neutrinos and search for new invisible states through the mono-photon process.
AI.method: Analyzing the process $e^+e^- 	o γν arν$ with full data from Belle II and using polarized beams to distinguish between contributions from neutral and charged currents.
AI.result: Belle II can determine the neutrino-sensitive effective weak mixing angle to a precision of 3.6%, comparable to other experimental methods, while polarized beams allow for independent analysis of neutrino interactions.
AI.conclusion: The process serves as a crucial background for dark boson searches, highlighting the significance of achieving high luminosity in $e^+e^-$ collisions.

title: Entangling capability of coherently controlled quantum processes
summary: We analytically characterize entanglement generation by two paradigmatic coherently controlled quantum processes, the quantum switch and time-flip. Retaining rather than measuring or discarding the control, we treat the control and target as the bipartite system and assume pure product inputs, so that any output entanglement reflects the entangling capability of the process. For the switch of qubit unitaries, we derive exact expressions for entanglement, together with a geometric characterization and a coherence-entanglement conservation relation. We then extend our analysis to binary random unitary, Pauli, amplitude damping, and generalized amplitude damping channels. We prove that switch of channels commuting under composition cannot entangle a separable input. Yet maximal entanglement is possible even with dissipation, e.g., an entanglement-breaking damping channel switched with a bit-flip can transform a product input into a maximally entangled state. For two generalized amplitude damping channels, a common stationary state prevents entanglement, while different stationary populations can enable it. We present an analogous study for the time-flip of unitary and binary random unitary channels. Our findings provide a systematic analysis of how much entanglement can be generated by coherent control of channel order or input-output direction.

AI.motivation: To understand how coherent control over quantum processes influences entanglement generation without the need to measure or discard control inputs.
AI.method: Using analytical techniques, the authors characterize entanglement generation in quantum switches and time-flips, deriving exact expressions and exploring various unitary and damping channels.
AI.result: The study shows that entanglement can be generated despite dissipation and that specific configurations of channels can either enable or prevent entanglement development.
AI.conclusion: The findings elucidate the potential for coherent control in enhancing entanglement generation, contributing significantly to the field of quantum information.

title: A NICER view of PSR J1614$-$2230: a massive and compact millisecond pulsar
comment: 27 pages, 11 figures and 5 tables. Submitted to ApJ. Data files available in Zenodo
summary: Using pulse profile modeling, we obtain the mass-radius measurement of a millisecond pulsar (MSP) with data from the Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR, XMM-Newton and the Chandra X-ray Observatory. We report here the radius of PSR J1614$-$2230, the second most massive MSP confirmed by radio timing. All of the data sets are well described by a simple model composed of two circular hot spots. The final result yields an equatorial radius of $R_{\rm eq}=10.06 ^{+1.25}_{-0.87}\,$km, and a gravitational mass of $M=1.937^{+0.012}_{-0.013}\,M_{\odot}$ (equally tailed 68% credible intervals). Although a non-thermal component was previously reported at higher energies, we find no sign of it in either our phase-averaged or phase-resolved spectral analyses. Using new relations linking the compactness to oblateness or surface gravity, and tailored to the spin frequency of PSR J1614$-$2230, we infer a configuration with one hot spot near the pole, and another near the equator. The tight mass posterior is essentially informed by radio timing, while the radius constraint is not as tight due to the low source signal (8.5$σ$ X-ray pulse significance). However, over all geometries and atmosphere models tested, the radius posterior tends toward low values ($\lesssim12.08\,$km, 90th percentile in all cases).

AI.method: Pulse profile modeling analyzed data from Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR, XMM-Newton, and Chandra to measure the radius and mass, employing a model with two circular hot spots.

title: Detectability-Aware Screening of Post-Merger Gravitational-Wave Damping Anomalies in Real Detector Noise: A Graph-Spectral Approach with Empirical Null Calibration
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to RAS Techniques and Instruments. Code and reproducibility materials available at https://github.com/ruslanalas/gw-postmerger-detectability and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21993621
summary: A two-stage methodological proof of concept for screening simplified post-merger gravitational-wave damping anomalies in real LIGO Livingston noise is presented. The injected signal is a controlled damped-sinusoid proxy rather than a physically complete binary-neutron-star post-merger waveform; it is used to test statistical detectability and damping-time scoring under real-noise calibration. Stage 1 constructs a local time-frequency graph from Constant-Q representations of whitened candidate windows and uses the leading eigenvalue as a detectability statistic, with its null distribution calibrated empirically on real detector noise. Stage 2 estimates an effective damping-time score for Stage-1-passing candidates using nonlinear least squares and an interpretable ridge/energy-decay estimator, with thresholds fixed before final held-out evaluation. The matched-filter SNR convention is checked with synthetic Gaussian noise, while the graph statistic is assessed through power-comparison and tile-shuffling tests. On a held-out real-noise test block, the nonlinear least-squares Stage-2 score gives AUC = 0.943 and TPR = 0.879 at FPR = 0.012, outperforming a calibrated power-only baseline.

AI.motivation: The study aims to enhance the detectability of gravitational-wave events, specifically post-merger cases, by utilizing simplified models to assess real detector noise.
AI.method: The methodology includes a two-stage process: Stage 1 uses a local time-frequency graph and leading eigenvalue as a detectability statistic, while Stage 2 employs nonlinear least squares for damping-time estimation.
AI.result: The approach achieves an AUC of 0.943 and a TPR of 0.879 at a low FPR of 0.012 on real noise data, showing improved performance over traditional methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed two-stage method successfully identifies damping anomalies, establishing a robust framework for future gravitational-wave analysis.

title: Fabrication and characterization of lithium-diffused inverted coaxial point-contact HPGe detectors
summary: High-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors with low capacitance, low electronic noise, and stable high-voltage operation are important for high-resolution gamma-ray spectroscopy and rare-event searches. We report the fabrication and characterization of two compact p-type inverted coaxial point-contact (ICPC) HPGe detectors, AK01 and AK02, produced from crystals grown at the University of South Dakota. Both devices use lithium-diffused $n^{+}$ outer contacts together with amorphous-Ge/Al point-contact electrodes. The principal advance is the implementation of this hybrid contact process on two independently fabricated USD-grown ICPC prototypes and the demonstration of stable electrical and spectroscopic operation. Both detectors exhibited picoampere-level leakage currents, operational depletion-voltage ranges of approximately 200--250~V (AK01) and 240--260~V (AK02), and estimated effective plateau capacitances of approximately 0.84 and 0.87~pF, respectively. Measurements with a $^{137}$Cs source yielded archived full-energy-peak FWHM values of 1.71 and 1.62~keV near 662~keV for AK01 and AK02, while AK02 yielded 1.04~keV FWHM at 59.5~keV with $^{241}$Am. Electric-field calculations reproduce the expected ICPC field configuration for the measured detector geometry. A Geant4 model of AK02 is used as a qualitative response study; its 0.8-mm Li-diffused inactive layer is an illustrative model assumption rather than a measured thickness, and its Gaussian broadening is constrained by the experimental resolution. The work therefore establishes the fabrication and operation of compact lithium-diffused ICPC prototypes while identifying quantitative inactive-layer characterization as an important next step.

AI.tldr: This paper details the development of compact p-type inverted coaxial point-contact HPGe detectors, focusing on their fabrication, electrical performance, and spectroscopic applications.
AI.motivation: To enhance high-resolution gamma-ray spectroscopy and facilitate rare-event searches through improved HPGe detectors.
AI.method: Fabrication and characterization of two ICPC HPGe detectors (AK01 and AK02), using lithium-diffused n+ contacts and amorphous-Ge/Al electrodes, followed by electrical and spectroscopic testing with radioactive sources.
AI.result: Both detectors showed stable operation with very low leakage currents and effective capacitances, achieving full-energy-peak FWHM values of 1.71 and 1.62 keV for AK01 and AK02, respectively, along with promising electric field configurations.
AI.conclusion: The successful fabrication and characterization of these compact detectors pave the way for further enhancements and highlight the importance of accurately quantifying inactive-layer thickness in future studies.

title: Construction and Performance of the sMDT Precision Muon Tracking Chambers for ATLAS at the HL-LHC
summary: In order to improve the muon trigger efficiency and the rate capability of the ATLAS muon detectors for operation at the high luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), the Monitored Drift Tube (MDT) tracking chambers in the inner barrel layer of the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer will be replaced by small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers integrated with new thin-gap RPC trigger chambers. The sMDT chambers are in serial production since January 2021. This documentation provides insight into the drift tube production and every step performed in the chamber construction at the MPI Munich. The serial production involves a stringent quality control program to assure the reliability and high mechanical precision of the chambers. This program consists of tests of the individual drift tubes, measurements of the chamber geometry and proof of gas tightness. Final certification at the production site is provided using cosmic rays. The dedicated quality control database and monitoring Web interface that is used commonly for both production sites of the sMDT chambers is presented

AI.tldr: This paper details the production and quality control processes of small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers for ATLAS muon detectors, aimed at enhancing trigger efficiency during the HL-LHC upgrade.
AI.motivation: To enhance the muon trigger efficiency and manage the rate capabilities at the HL-LHC, a replacement of the existing MDT tracking chambers is necessary.
AI.method: The sMDT chambers are produced with a stringent quality control program at MPI Munich, including tests for individual drift tubes, geometry measurements, gas tightness verification, and final certification using cosmic rays.
AI.result: Insights into the production processes and quality control measures, including the development of a dedicated quality control database and monitoring interface for sMDT production.
AI.conclusion: The implementation of the quality control program ensures the reliability and mechanical precision of the sMDT chambers for high-performance operation during the HL-LHC.

title: Searching for Axions on a Higher Note: Third-Harmonic Generation from Colliding High-Intensity Laser Beams
summary: We propose a new laboratory strategy to generate and detect axion-like particles via third-harmonic generation induced by two non-collinear, polarised high-intensity laser beams of peak intensity of the order of $10^{24}\,\mathrm{W/cm^2}$, where the third-harmonic signal is generated by the axion field. Starting from the axion-modified Maxwell equations, we analytically derive the axion-induced third-harmonic field, and show that by using state-of-the-art petawatt laser facilities, a detectable signal can be obtained over a broad range of axion masses and couplings. A key feature of the setup is that the axion-photon conversion rate can be resonantly enhanced by tuning the angle between the two beams through a mechanism that does not depend on the physical volume of the apparatus. The proposed configuration may therefore probe an unexplored region of axion parameter space and pave the way for next-generation high-power laser-based axion searches.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a strategy to detect axion-like particles using high-intensity laser beams, focusing on third-harmonic generation.
AI.motivation: To explore the existence of axion-like particles and probe unexplored axion parameter space.
AI.method: Utilizing two non-collinear, polarized high-intensity laser beams to induce a detectable third-harmonic signal through axion-photon conversion.
AI.result: Analytical derivation of the axion-induced third-harmonic field, demonstrating potential detectability over a range of axion masses and couplings.
AI.conclusion: The strategy may enhance axion detection capabilities and contribute to next-generation laser-based searches.

title: Exact learning of quantum noise with tensor networks
summary: Accurate noise models are essential for high-performance quantum error correction, yet characterizing the noise of a quantum device typically requires dedicated experiments. We present a variational framework that learns the noise model directly from quantum-error-correction syndrome and logical-observable data collected during error-corrected memory experiments. The fault-event probabilities are treated as variational parameters and optimized via gradient descent to minimize the binary cross-entropy between the decoder's predictions and experimental logical-observable outcomes. We prove that this objective is principled rather than ad hoc: a sufficiently expressive noise ansatz attains the information-theoretic minimum logical error rate. We instantiate this framework using a tensor-network decoder, which provides exact maximum-likelihood decoding and analytically differentiable gradients with respect to all noise parameters. Using circuit-level data from Google's Sycamore processor, and starting from an uninformed prior, the optimization recovers noise models whose logical error rates agree to within $2\%$ with those of Google's independently characterized detector error model. The mean squared error between the learned and reference noise parameters shows a clear overall decrease throughout training, confirming that the method recovers physically meaningful noise structure, not merely parameters that happen to decode well. We further demonstrate that the optimization can track device drifts in real time via warm-started updates, maintaining near-optimal decoding performance under synthetically evolving noise without the need for re-characterization. The approach is decoder-agnostic in its formulation and naturally extends to correlated noise models.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a variational method for learning noise models in quantum error correction using syndrome and logical-observable data, achieving high accuracy and real-time adaptation without re-characterization.
AI.motivation: Characterizing noise accurately is crucial for effective quantum error correction, yet conventional methods often necessitate specialized experiments.
AI.method: The authors introduce a variational framework that optimizes fault-event probabilities using gradient descent to minimize the binary cross-entropy between predictions and experimental outcomes, employing a tensor-network decoder for precise maximum-likelihood decoding.
AI.result: The optimization yields noise models matching Google's detector error model within 2% accuracy and shows consistent decreases in mean squared error across training, indicating recovery of meaningful noise structures.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework is decoder-agnostic, capable of adapting to evolving noise characteristics in real-time without requiring repeated characterization.

title: Equation of state and neutron star properties with new mass-radius constraints from PSR~J1614--2230, PSR~J2124--3358, and 47~Tuc~X7
summary: We study the impact of new mass-radius information from PSR J1614-2230, PSR J2124-3358, and 47 Tuc X7 in a combined equation of state inference based on chiral effective field theory constraints at nuclear densities and using different high-density extensions, including perturbative QCD constraints. The largest impact stems from the heavy-mass PSR J1614-2230 star, which shifts heavy neutron stars to smaller radii by around 0.4 km. Moreover, the combined astrophysical NICER, LIGO/Virgo, and X-ray information drives the radius posterior to a more data-driven distribution, which is less sensitive to the high-density extension. For the equation of state, the new mass-radius information significantly tightens the pressure and speed-of-sound posterior distributions, especially around three times saturation density. Finally, we make predictions for the poorly constrained masses of PSR J2124-3358 and 47 Tuc X7 based on the combined equation of state analysis and the other astrophysical sources.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates how new mass-radius data from specific pulsars influences the equation of state (EoS) for neutron stars, emphasizing improved constraints on pressure and sound speed at nuclear densities.
AI.motivation: To incorporate recent mass-radius measurements from pulsars into the equation of state inference for neutron stars, which can refine our understanding of their properties under extreme conditions.
AI.method: The study combines mass-radius data from PSR J1614-2230, PSR J2124-3358, and 47 Tuc X7 with constraints from chiral effective field theory and high-density extensions, including perturbative QCD, to analyze the EoS.
AI.result: Incorporating the new mass-radius information shifts the estimated radii of heavy neutron stars to smaller values and constrains the EoS more effectively, particularly around three times saturation density.
AI.conclusion: The research successfully narrows the uncertainties in neutron star characteristics and offers predictions for the masses of PSR J2124-3358 and 47 Tuc X7, based on a more refined equation of state.

title: The promise of self-supervised and active learning for Strong Lens discovery: Astronomaly applied to KiDS
comment: You can write: `Accepted for publication in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS).` If you also want to include the paper length/figures, for example: Accepted for publication in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS)
summary: Strong gravitational lenses (SGLs) are rare systems whose discovery currently relies primarily on supervised machine learning methods trained on large simulated datasets. We present the first application of Astronomaly:PROTEGE to SGL discovery, demonstrating that a human-in-the-loop active learning framework can efficiently identify lenses in large imaging surveys without the need for simulated training data. We consider a sample of 3.7 million bright galaxies from the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) DR4. Feature representations are extracted using a convolutional neural network pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on KiDS data using the self-supervised Bootstrap Your Own Latent (BYOL) framework. Within the embedding of these representations, the active learning loop of Astronomaly iteratively selects the most informative systems for expert inspection. A total of 3,000 objects are inspected across multiple rounds, yielding 34 high-quality (grade A/B) SGL candidates. On the basis that these systems occupy similar regions in the learned feature space, we expand this sample through nearest-neighbour similarity analysis. Including the active learning discoveries, we identify a total of 140 grade A/B candidates and more than 1,000 additional lower-confidence systems (grade C). Among the A/B candidates, 81 are newly identified, while approximately 22% of previously known grade A/B KiDS lenses are recovered. These results demonstrate strong potential for next-generation surveys such as Euclid, Roman, and Rubin's Legacy Survey of Space and Time. With approximately 60% of the high-quality candidates newly reported, this approach complements supervised methods by reducing reliance on simulations and enabling the discovery of a diverse population of SGLs.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel active learning approach for discovering strong gravitational lenses (SGLs) using Astronomaly:PROTEGE, demonstrating its efficacy without reliance on simulated datasets.
AI.motivation: The goal is to improve the discovery of rare strong gravitational lenses (SGLs) beyond traditional supervised machine learning methods that heavily depend on simulated data.
AI.method: The study utilizes a human-in-the-loop active learning framework, applying a convolutional neural network pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned on KiDS data to iteratively select and inspect the most informative galaxy systems for SGL identification.
AI.result: The method identified 34 high-quality SGL candidates and expanded the total to 140 grade A/B candidates, with 81 being newly discovered and 22% of previously known lenses being recovered.
AI.conclusion: This approach reduces reliance on simulations and is promising for upcoming astronomical surveys, enhancing the discovery of a diverse population of strong gravitational lenses.

title: Superconducting Flux Memory for Cryogenic Applications
summary: We report the development of flux memory for use with superconducting circuits. This technology stores persistent currents in superconducting loops on-chip to be used to provide flux biasing for superconducting circuits, like qubits. We developed three types of flux memory and draw comparisons among them for circuit design. We demonstrate the utility of flux memory by using an in-situ flux detector and characterize each approach and further demonstrate that once flux is set in a memory cell, benchtop DC control sources can be powered off, leaving the on-chip flux bias in place. We propose that flux memory can be arranged in a two-dimensional configuration to multiplex control signals and reduce how line counts scale (N^2 devices -> 2N control lines), and our experimental results pave the path to the proposed scalability. We demonstrate the use of flux memory to flux bias a transmon qubit and show the tunability of the qubit state to a target frequency which remained stable on-chip for 20 hours.

AI.tldr: Development of on-chip flux memory for superconducting circuits, enabling persistent current storage, with demonstrated applications in qubit biasing.
AI.motivation: To enhance control and biasing of superconducting circuits by utilizing flux memory, addressing the challenges of circuit design and scalability.
AI.method: Three types of flux memory were developed and characterized using an in-situ flux detector, demonstrating persistence of stored flux with powered-off control sources.
AI.result: Flux memory successfully flux biases a transmon qubit, achieving stable tunability of the qubit state for 20 hours.
AI.conclusion: The development of flux memory enables multiplexed control signals and paves the way for improved scalability in superconducting circuits.

title: The recasting bound atlas on pair production of vector-like quarks
summary: We present a comprehensive recasting study of pair production of vector-like quarks. We consider decays of vector-like quarks into third generation quarks and Standard Model bosons or exotic top-philic scalars. We derive recasting bounds on all 43 combinations of decay channels. Using the efficiencies of each channel, we obtain combined limits across decay channels by adding up the contributions to each signal region. A data base of recasting results along with example codes is published, allowing for application to different models without the need for rerunning recasting tools. We demonstrate the utility of the data base by setting bounds on several sample models.

AI.tldr: The study focuses on recasting decay channels of vector-like quarks and establishes bounds across various combinations, providing a database for practical applications in model analysis.
AI.motivation: To analyze the decay processes of vector-like quarks and provide a systematic approach to derive recasting limits for various decay combinations.
AI.method: The authors derived recasting bounds on 43 combinations of decay channels, calculating efficiencies and combining limits for signal regions, while publishing an accessible database of results and example codes.
AI.result: Combined limits across decay channels demonstrate the effectiveness of using a data-driven approach to analyze vector-like quark models.
AI.conclusion: The database enables researchers to apply the results to different models efficiently, establishing a foundational resource for further studies.

title: Quantum Secret Sharing with a Helper and Programmable Access Structures
summary: Quantum secret sharing (QSS) is a process in which the state of a quantum system is partitioned into multiple shares, allowing only specific subsets of shareholders to reconstruct the state, while others gain no information about its identity. In this work, we propose a variant of QSS, called ``helper QSS,'' which designates a special shareholder whose participation with any other group of parties is sufficient for recovering the state. We present different families of helper codes that function for an arbitrary number of parties and system sizes. As an application, we introduce the idea of a programmable access structure in QSS, which allows for a third-party programmer to independently choose the access structure of the code even after the shares are delivered to all the shareholders. This choice is made blindly, meaning that the programmer has no information about the secret being encoded, and it is implemented using the nonlocal process of quantum steering.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a variant of quantum secret sharing (QSS) known as helper QSS, which enables recovery of a quantum state with the help of a designated shareholder, along with the concept of programmable access structures that can be defined post-share distribution.
AI.motivation: To enhance the capabilities and flexibility of quantum secret sharing by allowing a designated helper to assist in state recovery and enabling post-distribution programmable access structures.
AI.method: The authors propose helper QSS where a specific shareholder aids in the recovery of quantum states. They develop various families of helper codes applicable for different party configurations. Additionally, the concept of a programmable access structure is introduced, allowing third-party programmers to define access post-share delivery using quantum steering processes.
AI.result: Families of helper codes are presented, demonstrating versatility across multiple parties and system sizes. The idea of programmable access structures is successfully illustrated, highlighting the ability to maintain confidentiality while allowing flexible access definitions.
AI.conclusion: Helper QSS offers a robust framework for improved quantum secret sharing, emphasizing flexibility in access structures without compromising the security of the encoded secret.

title: GRMHD Simulations of Accreting Proto-Magnetars I. Implications for Gamma-Ray Burst Jets and Energetic Explosions
summary:
Newly formed, rapidly rotating, strongly magnetized neutron stars ("millisecond proto-magnetars") are promising central engines for gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and luminous supernovae. Although often modeled in isolation, they can be born surrounded by accretion disks in stellar collapse, neutron-star mergers, or accretion-induced collapse. We present axisymmetric GRMHD simulations of hyperaccretion onto such objects, including a physical equation of state and charged-current weak interactions. Holding the weakly magnetized accretion torus fixed, we vary the stellar dipole field strength to span crushed-magnetosphere, magnetically channeled accretion, and centrifugal-propeller regimes, and compare with an otherwise similar accreting black hole.
  Accretion compresses the stellar magnetosphere and opens additional magnetic flux, producing relativistic jet powers that exceed isolated-dipole spin-down estimates by factors of a few to ~10. Even while the magnetosphere remains compressed against the stellar surface, stronger fields increasingly impede accretion and enhance outflows. Channeled-accretion models show strong jet variability driven by plasmoid eruptions and intermittent magnetospheric accretion, whereas the propeller model produces a steadier, more powerful jet and rapid spin-down. The disk-magnetosphere interaction also regulates how efficiently the neutron star grows and whether it spins up or down; near spin equilibrium, inefficient accretion can delay collapse to a black hole relative to estimates based on the external mass-supply rate. Accreting proto-magnetars can therefore power relativistic jets and baryon-rich outflows with energetics comparable to those inferred for long GRBs and GRB-supernovae. A companion paper explores implications for neutron-rich ejecta and r-process nucleosynthesis.

AI.tldr: The study simulates hyperaccretion onto newly formed proto-magnetars, identifying how varying magnetic fields influence jet dynamics and accretion processes, with implications for gamma-ray bursts and nucleosynthesis.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of millisecond proto-magnetars in powerfully energetic astronomical events like gamma-ray bursts and supernovae, especially in their interactions with accretion disks during formation.
AI.method: Axisymmetric GRMHD simulations of hyperaccretion, varying stellar dipole field strengths while keeping the weakly magnetized torus fixed, including a realistic equation of state and charged-current weak interactions.
AI.result: Stronger magnetic fields compress the magnetosphere, increasing relativistic jet power; different magnetic regimes yield diverse jet variability and impact neutron star growth, spinning dynamics, and potential black hole formation.
AI.conclusion: Accreting proto-magnetars can produce relativistic jets and baryon-rich outflows with energies comparable to those seen in long gamma-ray bursts and associated supernovae, highlighting their significance in cosmic phenomena.

title: Flux jump correction in the QUBIC TES data pipeline
summary: Flux jumps occur in the readout electronics of Transition Edge Sensor (TES) detectors coupled to Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs), as a consequence of the periodic transfer function of SQUIDs in the superconducting regime. These events manifest as discontinuities in the Time Ordered Data (TOD) and can significantly degrade the quality of the measured signals. In this work, we present an automated pipeline to identify and correct flux jumps in the calibration data of the QUBIC (Q \& U Bolometric Interferometer for Cosmology) instrument, designed to measure the B-mode polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Using data from multiple observation campaigns, we characterize the statistical properties of flux jumps and compare them with expectations based on the electronic configuration of the instrument. The proposed pipeline successfully corrects these events, allowing the recovery of affected data and enabling their use in subsequent CMB analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses flux jumps in TES detectors coupled to SQUIDs, impacting data quality in cosmological measurements, and presents an automated correction pipeline.
AI.motivation: Flux jumps degrade signal quality in TES detectors linked to SQUIDs, affecting the calibration data of instruments like QUBIC that measure CMB polarization.
AI.method: An automated pipeline was developed to identify and correct flux jumps in calibration data, utilizing data from various observation campaigns to analyze statistical properties of these events.
AI.result: The pipeline effectively corrects flux jumps, allowing recovery of compromised data for enhanced reliability in CMB analysis.
AI.conclusion: Correcting flux jumps improves data quality, enabling more accurate cosmological observations and analyses.

title: Dynamics and Frequency Conversion of Accreting Axion Clouds
summary: Axion fields can form exponentially growing gravitational clouds around compact objects through self-interaction-driven relaxation of ambient axion waves. As the field amplitude approaches the axion decay constant, nonlinear effects become important. We identify two distinct regimes of late-time evolution, determined by the gravitational fine-structure constant and the cloud growth rate: a Bosenova regime, characterized by collapse accompanied by explosive axion bursts, and a saturation regime, in which self-interaction-induced axion emission balances accretion. In the latter regime, the emitted axion radiation exhibits stable discrete spectral lines at odd multiples of the bound-state energy, directly probing the global structure of the axion potential beyond its quadratic minimum. We show that single-cosine potentials and QCD axion-like potentials predict distinct emission spectra, enabling probes of the underlying axion self-interaction structure and its ultraviolet completion through terrestrial detection of relativistic axion fluxes from compact objects.

AI.tldr: Axion fields can create gravitational clouds around compact objects through relaxation mechanisms, leading to two evolutionary regimes: explosive collapse (Bosenova) and stable emission balance (saturation). Emission spectra differ based on the axion potential's form.
AI.motivation: Understanding the late-time behavior of axion fields can provide insights into their role in astrophysical processes and their fundamental interactions.
AI.method: The paper analyzes the dynamics of axion clouds around compact objects, categorizing their late-time evolution into two regimes based on gravitational interactions and emission properties.
AI.result: Identified two regimes: the Bosenova regime shows explosive bursts, while the saturation regime features stable spectral lines linked to axion potentials.
AI.conclusion: Differences in emission spectra from various axion potentials allow for experimental probes of axions and their underlying interactions in astrophysical settings.

title: Codes for Quantum Secret Sharing with a Helper
summary: Helper quantum secret sharing is a form of secret sharing defined by its unique access structure. One special fixed party, called the helper, can work together with any other party to fully decode the secret. A blind helper is one who can provide this assistance while not holding any local information about the encoded secret. In this work, we analyze the general structure of QSS helper codes and present new code constructions. We fully characterize the structure of blind helper stabilizer codes and show that for the encoding of a single qubit, recovery is always possible using one-way local operations and classical communication (LOCC) from the helper to the targeted party. Furthermore, we demonstrate how such codes also allow for the helper to target larger subsets of parties by one-way LOCC, enabling them to be authorized to recover the secret. Finally, when each party only holds a qubit, we identify the general form of all helper codes (including non-stabilizer codes) and find that LOCC recovery is only possible in special cases.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes helper quantum secret sharing (QSS) codes, focusing on blind helper stabilizer codes and their recovery methods.
AI.motivation: To explore and improve the structure and capabilities of quantum secret sharing codes, particularly in the context of blind helpers who lack local information about the secret.
AI.method: The authors characterize blind helper stabilizer codes and present new code constructions, investigating recovery methods using one-way local operations and classical communication (LOCC).
AI.result: Recovery from a blind helper is always feasible for single qubit encoding using LOCC; larger subsets of parties can also be targeted for recovery, but general helper codes may have limited LOCC recovery.
AI.conclusion: While helper quantum secret sharing codes are versatile, LOCC recovery is constrained to specific configurations, particularly when parties hold only one qubit.

title: Evidence for a luminosity-class dichotomy in the supergiant donors of persistent high-mass X-ray binaries and supergiant fast X-ray transients
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (received May 18, 2026; accepted August 11, 2026). The manuscript comprises 11 pages, 5 figures, and 4 tables. The version submitted here also includes all supplementary tables (B.1, C.1, C.2, and D.1), which in the published A&A article are provided exclusively in electronic form via the CDS
summary: We have investigated the properties of the supergiant donors in two types of high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs, i.e. the so-called supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) and the classical X-ray sources), by collecting all available information from the literature. A prevalence of O-type versus B-type supergiant donors in SFXTs was previously suggested in the literature, possibly indicative of faster winds in SFXTs than in classical, persistent sources. Our aim is to investigate whether there is evidence for a dichotomy in the stellar luminosity class, since B-type supergiants are also known to be hosted in SFXTs. Our collection of the relevant literature allowed us to build a robust sample of both types of HMXBs with a secure stellar classification. We have found that the SFXTs showing the most extreme, transient X-ray emission host only O-type or B-type stars with a Ib and Iab luminosity class, whereas classical sources have mostly Ia donors. This is robust evidence that might explain the two different behaviours of HMXBs at X-rays since the stellar luminosity class appears to be linked to the wind properties (the supergiant wind terminal velocity, the mass-loss rate, and the wind strength Q parameter), indicative of faster and less dense winds in SFXTs than in classical sources.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the properties of supergiant donors in high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) and finds that supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) mainly host lower luminosity class stars compared to classical X-ray sources, implying a significant link between stellar properties and X-ray emissions.
AI.motivation: To explore differences in properties of supergiant donors in SFXTs and classical HMXBs, focusing on their stellar luminosity classes.
AI.method: A literature review was conducted to compile a dataset of supergiant donors with secure classifications in SFXTs and classical HMXBs.
AI.result: SFXTs mostly host O-type or B-type supergiants with luminosity classes Ib and Iab, while classical sources predominantly feature Ia donors, indicating a link between these classes and their X-ray emission behaviors.
AI.conclusion: The study provides robust evidence that the differences in X-ray emissions between SFXTs and classical sources may be attributed to the differing wind properties associated with the stellar luminosity classes.

title: Simulation and development of astrophotonic H-band nulling beam combiner for the CHARA Array
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, SPIE Astronomical Telescopes and Instrumentation proceeding submitted to "Optical and Infrared Interferometry and Imaging X"
summary: Nulling interferometry is a promising method for direct detection and characterization of faint stellar companions such as exoplanets and faint binary sources. The dominant constraint on instrument performance is instability noise from vibrations, thermal expansions, and other systematic sources. Photonic instruments have footprints of a few centimeters and enable advanced light control architectures. Astrophotonic implementations can include active phase control via Mach-Zehnder interferometers (MZIs) to actively minimize residual optical path errors at the location of beam combination. The compact size of photonic chips also makes them a promising solution for space-based applications such as the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory. The Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array is equipped with the world's longest baseline in the near-infrared at 330 meters long. CHARA therefore has the most sensitive angular resolution in the near-infrared. A nuller at CHARA would have access to a novel parameter space essential for exoplanet discovery and characterization. The first step in preparing a nulling beam combiner for CHARA is to develop compelling, realistic, and well-defined science cases. Simulation suites quantify the technical requirements to reach such science goals in their respective complex systems. The CHARA Array Response Model (CHARM) is the first-ever simulator built specifically for CHARA, opening up new pathways for instrument simulation.
