For the class of potentials considered, we show that the differential scattering cross section is equivalent to that obtained in standard complex quantum mechanics. We also show that the tunneling probability in real quantum mechanics is identical to that in complex quantum mechanics.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an evolution equation in real quantum mechanics, establishing scattering and tunneling analogies with complex quantum mechanics.
AI.motivation: To understand scattering and tunneling in real quantum mechanics and establish parallels with complex formulations.
AI.method: Derivation of an evolution equation in real Kähler space, analogizing Stone's theorem, and examining scattering and tunneling through real wave operators and the S-matrix.
AI.result: The differential scattering cross section and tunneling probability in real quantum mechanics match those in standard complex quantum mechanics.
AI.conclusion: Real quantum mechanics displays consistent scattering and tunneling behaviors relative to complex quantum mechanics.

title: Addendum: Production of $π^{+} π^{-}$ pairs in diffractive photon-proton and in proton-proton collisions revisited, in particular concerning the Drell-Söding contribution
summary: We update our analyses concerning the non-resonant (Drell-Söding) contribution to the reaction $γ^{(*)} p \to π^{+} π^{-} p$, now including general vertex functions for the coupling of pomeron, $f_{2 \mathbb{R}}$, and $ρ_{\mathbb{R}}$, to pions. This takes into account the off-shellness of the pions. We present a comparison of our tensor-pomeron model, including our new Drell-Söding and $ρ$, $ω$ vector-meson contributions, with data for the $γp \to π^{+} π^{-} p$ reaction measured by the ZEUS and H1 Collaborations. We find very good agreement of our theory with the experimental data for the $π^{+} π^{-}$ invariant mass ($M_{ππ}$) and for angular distributions. Here we restrict our analysis to the region $M_{ππ} \lesssim 1.2$ GeV. For higher values of $M_{ππ}$ we will have to consider production of higher-mass mesons. The purpose of the present article is to show that our tensor-pomeron model gives a very good fit to the so-called skewing of the $ρ$-resonance contribution in photoproduction. In fact, it is an old problem/puzzle to understood the difference of the shapes of the $M_{ππ}$ distributions in the region of the $ρ(770)$ resonance in $e^{+} e^{-}$ annihilation and photoproduction. We think that with our results we have obtained for this problem a solution which is very satisfactory from the Quantum-Field-Theory point of view. Our results are also relevant for central-exclusive $π^{+} π^{-}$ production in ultraperipheral $pp$, A$p$, and AA collisions at the LHC and for photo- and electroproduction of $π^{+} π^{-}$ at future electron-proton/ion colliders, EIC and LeHC.

AI.tldr: This paper updates the analysis of the non-resonant Drell-Söding contribution to the reaction $γ^{(*)} p \to π^{+} π^{-} p$, incorporating vertex functions and comparing the tensor-pomeron model against experimental data, revealing strong agreement for $M_{ππ} < 1.2$ GeV.
AI.motivation: The study addresses discrepancies in the $M_{ππ}$ distributions observed between $e^{+} e^{-}$ annihilation and photoproduction, particularly concerning the skewing of the $ρ$-resonance contribution.
AI.method: The authors employ a tensor-pomeron model with newly incorporated Drell-Söding and vector-meson contributions, focusing on the non-resonant processes and considering off-shell pions.
AI.result: The model exhibits excellent agreement with experimental data for invariant mass and angular distributions in the low-energy region ($M_{ππ} < 1.2$ GeV), successfully addressing the skewness issue of the $ρ$-resonance.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide a satisfactory solution to a long-standing problem in Quantum Field Theory and extend implications for future particle collision studies, particularly in ultra-peripheral collisions and future colliders.

title: A continuous-mode quantum-optical representation of finite strong-field laser pulses in free space
summary: We formulate an energy-consistent quantum-optical representation of finite paraxial laser pulses in free space. The formulation is based on a continuous-mode description and provides a step toward a unified treatment of coherent and nonclassical strong-field drivers. Starting from plane-wave quantization, we construct a transverse vector-mode reduction in which the selected mode can reproduce an arbitrary normalized spatial--polarization profile. For a coherent pulse, the measured pulse energy and full laboratory analytic signal determine the frequency-dependent coherent-state displacement $(α(ω))$, without introducing a physical quantization volume. For nonclassical pulses, the same first-order field data and total energy do not uniquely specify the quantum state. Additional correlation information or model assumptions are required. We incorporate this information through normal and anomalous covariance kernels and discuss $g^{(2)}$-based diagnostics of squeezed pulses. We also derive a phase-sensitive convergence criterion for numerical frequency-bin discretizations. An exactly solvable continuum-mode free-electron application shows that the coherent displacement reproduces the semiclassical mean trajectory, whereas the field covariances determine the electron wave packet width. The framework offers a convenient, energy-consistent interface between measured free-space pulses and quantum-optical calculations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an energy-consistent quantum-optical framework for analyzing finite laser pulses in free space, integrating coherent and nonclassical pulse descriptions.
AI.motivation: To unify the treatment of coherent and nonclassical strong-field drivers in quantum optics, improving the understanding of laser pulse characteristics.
AI.method: The method involves a continuous-mode description starting from plane-wave quantization, leading to a transverse vector-mode reduction that adapts to arbitrary spatial-polarization profiles. It utilizes field data and energy measurements to assess coherent states and employs covariance kernels for nonclassical states.
AI.result: The approach allows for a summary of coherent states via energy metrics while showing that nonclassical states require additional information for precise characterization. A free-electron application illustrates the framework's effectiveness in linking coherent displacement to semiclassical trajectories.
AI.conclusion: The developed framework offers a comprehensive interface for connecting experimental data on free-space laser pulses with quantum-optical models, enhancing the analysis of their quantum characteristics.

title: On the Nature of $X(2370)$
summary: Recently, the BESIII Collaboration claimed that their observed $X(2370)$ ($J^{PC}=0^{-+}$) is predominantly a glueball state based on several arguments. However, we find these arguments to be flawed and the conclusion unjustified. Instead, we demonstrate that all observed properties of the $X(2370)$ can be naturally explained by a $\barΣΣ$ molecule dominated state.

AI.tldr: The paper critiques the BESIII Collaboration's claim that the $X(2370)$ is a glueball, arguing it is instead a $ arΣΣ$ molecule state.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the validity of the BESIII Collaboration's claim about the $X(2370)$ being a glueball state.
AI.method: Analyze the properties of the $X(2370)$ and compare them with predictions for both glueball and $ arΣΣ$ molecule states.
AI.result: Findings suggest that the observed properties align more closely with a $ arΣΣ$ molecule dominated state than with a glueball state.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion drawn by BESIII is unjustified, and the $X(2370)$ should be viewed as a $ arΣΣ$ molecule.

title: Quantum time-flip beats adaptive metrology: Asymptotic benefit, activation, and unsimulability
summary: In quantum metrology, adaptive and causal-superposition strategies are proven to be beneficial over parallel schemes for a finite number of channel uses, but their advantages disappear in the asymptotic limit. We show that quantum operations with indefinite time direction, specifically, time-flip (TF)-assisted strategies, referred to as indefinite time-directed metrology (ITDM), can overcome this asymptotic equivalence. Using semidefinite programming, we rigorously demonstrate that TF-assisted protocols can achieve quantum Fisher information (QFI) strictly exceeding the maximum value attainable by parallel, adaptive, and causal-superposition strategies, both for finite and asymptotically many channel uses. Moreover, we identify a class of Pauli noise channels for which ITDM achieves Heisenberg scaling, while all parallel, adaptive, and causal-superposition strategies remain restricted to standard scaling. We call this phenomenon as metrological activation. Interestingly, this activation can be used to exhibit that the quantum time-flip and transposition supermaps cannot be simulated by conventional quantum circuits or causal-superposition strategies using any finite number of channel queries, thereby establishing indefinite time direction as a genuine resource for quantum metrology.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces indefinite time-directed metrology (ITDM) with time-flip (TF) strategies, which surpasses traditional quantum metrology techniques in both finite and infinite channel uses.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of existing quantum metrology strategies (adaptive, parallel, causal-superposition) that fail to maintain advantages in the asymptotic limit.
AI.method: The authors employ semidefinite programming to analyze TF-assisted protocols, demonstrating their effectiveness in exceeding quantum Fisher information (QFI) when compared to other strategies.
AI.result: ITDM exhibits quantum Fisher information that surpasses what is achievable by conventional strategies, and demonstrates Heisenberg scaling for specific Pauli noise channels.
AI.conclusion: Indefinite time direction is established as a valuable resource in quantum metrology, showcasing metrological activation that cannot be simulated by any standard quantum circuits.

title: Phase structure of magnetized quark matter at imaginary chemical potential
summary: We investigate the phase structure of magnetized quark matter within a nonlocal SU(2) Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model. Our work focuses on the interplay between temperature and imaginary chemical potential in the presence of an external uniform magnetic field, with emphasis on the deconfinement and Roberge-Weiss transitions. We analyze the dependence of the relevant critical temperatures on the external field, and we explore the sensitivity of the phase structure to different Polyakov loop effective potentials. Our results show qualitative agreement with lattice QCD findings, reproducing inverse magnetic catalysis in the chiral sector and a decreasing behavior of the Roberge-Weiss transition temperature with increasing magnetic field.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes magnetized quark matter using a nonlocal SU(2) Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model, focusing on temperature and imaginary chemical potential impacts on deconfinement and Roberge-Weiss transitions under an external magnetic field.
AI.motivation: To understand the phase behavior of magnetized quark matter, particularly how temperature and magnetic fields affect critical transitions in the system.
AI.method: Utilization of a nonlocal SU(2) Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model to study phase transitions regarding temperature, imaginary chemical potential, and magnetic fields.
AI.result: Findings reveal qualitative alignment with lattice QCD results, showing inverse magnetic catalysis in the chiral sector and a decrease in Roberge-Weiss transition temperature as the magnetic field increases.
AI.conclusion: The research demonstrates that the inclusion of an external magnetic field significantly influences the critical temperatures and phase transitions in quark matter.

title: Unbiased sampling from Boltzmann distributions with noisy energies
summary: Sampling from the Boltzmann distribution is central to computational physics, yet hard when the energy is known only through a stochastic estimate, such as with machine-learned molecular potentials, in variational Monte Carlo, or on quantum computers, because a noisy energy biases the sampled distribution. The penalty method of Ceperley and Dewing corrects this but requires the noise variance and becomes intractable when it is large. We introduce the Poisson product estimator, an unbiased, non-negative estimator of the Boltzmann weight that only needs an upper bound on the energy estimator and remains efficient at high noise. Using it to optimize a variational quantum circuit gradient-free, we recover the $H_3^+$ ground-state energy in a minimal basis and, by sampling rather than following a single trajectory, also map the variational energy landscape.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Poisson product estimator for efficient sampling from the Boltzmann distribution in the presence of noise, overcoming limitations of previous methods.
AI.motivation: The need for effective sampling in situations where energy estimates are stochastic, particularly in fields like quantum computing and variational Monte Carlo, drives this work.
AI.method: The Poisson product estimator is developed as an unbiased, non-negative approach that requires only an upper bound on energy estimates, making it robust against noise.
AI.result: Using the new estimator in a variational quantum circuit, the authors successfully recover the ground-state energy of $H_3^+$ and explore the energy landscape through sampling methods.
AI.conclusion: The Poisson product estimator is an effective and practical tool for Boltzmann sampling in noisy environments, enhancing computational efficiency in quantum applications.

title: Probing jet medium interaction with generalized projected energy correlators
summary: We study medium modifications to generalized projected energy correlators, referred to as $ν$-correlators, measured on jets in heavy-ion collisions. While the vacuum distributions of these correlators exhibit a characteristic $1/ν$ enhancement, we show that in a dense medium this behavior is regulated within both the BDMPS-Z and semi-classical approximations as $ν\to 0$. As a result, contributions from medium-induced emissions become parametrically suppressed relative to the vacuum baseline. We observe a similar trend in the simulated events generated with JEWEL. We find that while the large angle enhancement is qualitatively similar across different values of $ν$, the small angle distribution changes drastically between $ν<1$ and $ν>1$. This indicates that small angle modifications, primarily driven by jet energy loss, are imprinted differently across $ν$-correlators. In particular, for $ν<1$ the small angle enhancement is less prominent which suggests that these correlators may provide improved sensitivity to medium modifications in the large angle region.

AI.tldr: This study investigates how medium effects influence $ν$-correlators in jets during heavy-ion collisions, finding that medium-induced emissions suppress the expected vacuum behavior, especially in small angle distributions depending on the value of $ν$.
AI.motivation: Understanding jet modifications in heavy-ion collisions can provide insights into quark-gluon plasma properties and medium-induced emissions.
AI.method: Analyzed medium modifications to $ν$-correlators using BDMPS-Z and semi-classical approximations, supplemented by simulations from JEWEL.
AI.result: Medium-induced emissions are suppressed compared to vacuum distributions, with distinct behaviors noted in small angle distributions dependent on $ν$ values.
AI.conclusion: $ν$-correlators may be a better tool for probing medium effects in the large angle region, as small angle enhancements exhibit significant variations based on the $ν$ parameter.

title: Terrestrial Gravitational Wave Detection with Atom Interferometers
summary: Atom interferometers (AIFs) are highly precise inertial sensors and are considered promising instruments for the detection of gravitational waves (GWs) and certain dark matter (DM) candidates in the mid-frequency band. While GW detection with AIFs was initially proposed for space-based experiments with baselines spanning thousands of kilometers, recent developments suggest that terrestrial setups with baselines of at least 100 meters may also be capable of detecting GWs. In this work, we analytically derive the GW phase response formula of a ground detector, find an additional term compared to the existing literature and check it our findings numerically. Based on this treatment, we analyze the optimal geometric parameters for earth-bound AIF experiments. Subsequently, we numerically simulate GW detection schemes for these optimized interferometers using an open-source Python algorithm. Numerical simulations of these schemes have are not available to the community, yet crucial for the accurate modeling of noise and non-trivial gravitational backgrounds.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new analytical derivation of the gravitational wave (GW) phase response for terrestrial atom interferometers (AIFs), identifies additional terms compared to previous literature, and evaluates optimal geometric parameters for GW detection.
AI.motivation: The motivation lies in advancing the capability of atom interferometers for gravitational wave detection, especially by exploring terrestrial setups which are more feasible than space-based alternatives.
AI.method: The authors derive an analytical formula for the GW phase response in ground-based atom interferometers, identify additional response terms, and conduct numerical simulations using a Python algorithm to study various detection schemes and optimize geometric parameters.
AI.result: They discover an additional phase response term not previously addressed in other studies, and provide numerical simulations that enable a better understanding of noise and gravitational backgrounds in AIF detectors.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance the potential for terrestrial AIFs in GW detection and provide necessary simulations for improved experimental designs.

title: Inelastic Dark Matter Signature at High Recoil Energy in LUX-ZEPLIN and CRESST
summary: The LUX--ZEPLIN Collaboration recently reported one event at $E_{\mathrm{nr}}=248\pm23~\mathrm{keV}$ with an exposure of $2.84~\mathrm{tonne\cdot yr}$. In this Letter, we interpret this feature using endothermic dark matter (DM). We consider both direct scattering of the surviving ground-state halo component and the contribution of excited states produced by terrestrial upscattering. Our calculations show that explaining the high-energy event requires $m_χ\gtrsim500~\mathrm{GeV}$ and a mass splitting of $\mathcal{O}(300)~\mathrm{keV}$, for which the production of excited states inside the Earth is kinematically forbidden. For $\barσ_n=10^{-37}~\mathrm{cm^2}$, an illustrative two-bin likelihood analysis yields a representative best-fit point at $(m_χ,δ)\simeq(1.105~\mathrm{TeV},350~\mathrm{keV})$. The preferred parameter region may be tested by the planned CRESST upgrade.

AI.tldr: The study interprets a reported event in LUX-ZEPLIN through endothermic dark matter, requiring a dark matter mass of at least 500 GeV and a mass splitting around 300 keV, with implications for future testing.
AI.motivation: To explain a recent high-energy event detected by the LUX-ZEPLIN Collaboration using endothermic dark matter models.
AI.method: The study involves analyzing both direct scattering of ground-state halo particles and contributions from excited states due to terrestrial upscattering, utilizing a likelihood analysis.
AI.result: The analysis indicates that to explain the observed event, dark matter mass must be at least 500 GeV, with a mass splitting of approximately 300 keV, leading to a best-fit point of (m_χ,δ) ≈ (1.105 TeV, 350 keV).
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that the outlined parameters can be tested by upcoming upgrades to the CRESST experiment.

title: Anticoncentration and entanglement in Gaussian boson sampling
summary: Anticoncentration and entanglement are two properties used to study classical hardness or easiness of Gaussian boson sampling in varying regimes. In this paper, we consider three directions concerning anticoncentration and entanglement in Gaussian boson sampling: (1) We derive closed-form expressions for the second moment of hafnians of symmetric Gaussian products, and use this to precisely locate the anticoncentration transition as a function of the number of squeezed input modes. (2) We derive closed-form expressions for the Rényi-$α$ Page curves for Gaussian boson sampling. (3) We study unequal input squeezing parameters $(s_i)_i$, and prove estimates as well as monotonicity of the average-case Rényi-2 entropy Page curve in terms of the magnitudes $|s_i|$, which allow for extending equal squeezing results to unequal squeezing.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the interplay between anticoncentration and entanglement in Gaussian boson sampling through closed-form expressions for moments and Rényi entropy curves, while extending results to unequal squeezing.
AI.motivation: To investigate and clarify the roles of anticoncentration and entanglement in Gaussian boson sampling across different parameters.
AI.method: Derived closed-form expressions for moments of hafnians and Rényi-α Page curves, along with establishing properties for unequal input squeezing parameters.
AI.result: Closed-form expressions for second moments and Rényi-α Page curves were obtained, confirming the presence of anticoncentration transitions and establishing monotonicity of the Rényi-2 entropy curve under varying conditions.
AI.conclusion: The study enhances understanding of Gaussian boson sampling by providing new tools and results that apply to both equal and unequal input squeezing scenarios.

title: Gravitational Waves from Reheating beyond Instantaneous Thermalization
summary: We study gravitational-wave production during perturbative reheating without assuming instantaneous thermalization of the inflaton decay products. The injected energetic particles thermalize through an in-medium cascade of nearly collinear splittings subject to the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal effect and are ultimately isotropized by elastic scatterings near the thermal scale. The non-thermal hard population present before complete thermalization produces an additional gravitational-wave component through hard-soft scatterings, with $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}\propto f^{1/2}$ below the injection-scale turnover. The same isotropization erases the directional information underlying the vacuum $1/k$ bremsstrahlung soft pole, changing the deep-infrared spectrum from $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}\propto f$ to $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}\propto f^3$.

AI.tldr: This study examines gravitational waves generated during perturbative reheating without assuming instant thermalization of decay products, highlighting the effects of energetic particle cascades and isotropization on gravitational-wave spectra.
AI.motivation: To explore gravitational-wave production during the reheating phase of the universe with a more accurate treatment of particle thermalization.
AI.method: The authors analyze the thermalization process of energetic particles via in-medium cascade splittings and elastic scattering, considering the implications for gravitational-wave spectra.
AI.result: They find that non-thermal contributions lead to an additional gravitational-wave component, modifying the spectrum from $Ω_{	ext{GW}}	extpropto f$ to $Ω_{	ext{GW}} 	extpropto f^3$ in the deep infrared.
AI.conclusion: The research indicates that the isotropization during reheating is crucial in determining the characteristics of the resulting gravitational-wave background.

title: A Backend-Agnostic MWIS Kernel for Stochastic Unit Commitment with Neutral-Atom Hardware Validation
summary: Quantum hardware is beginning to address structured combinatorial optimisation, but two steps still block practical use: mapping real operational models onto hardware-compatible instances, and converting noisy hardware output back into feasible decisions. Here we introduce a backend-agnostic computational interface that compiles the discrete decision layer of stochastic unit commitment into a move-based maximum-weight independent set (MWIS) problem, while retaining continuous dispatch and feasibility recovery in the classical computational layer. We validate the approach in a green hydrogen scheduling setting and deploy it on the QuEra Aquila neutral-atom quantum processor. This is the first end-to-end industrial scheduling workflow that connects real operational decisions to programmable neutral-atom hardware through a solver-agnostic MWIS representation. Across a 15-day hardware campaign on 50-node instances, hardware-generated solutions after classical refinement match or exceed the dispatch margins obtained from exact MWIS on every day. When scaling to 144 nodes, encoding quality remains stable, while the probability that the full atom array survives, rather than graph embedding, emerges as the dominant bottleneck to further scaling. Together, these results establish a hardware-compatible computational pathway toward larger problem scales, and lay the groundwork for exploring regimes in which exact classical optimisation may no longer scale efficiently.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a backend-agnostic interface for mapping combinatorial optimization problems onto quantum hardware, demonstrated in green hydrogen scheduling.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges of efficiently using quantum hardware for structured combinatorial optimization problems in real-world applications.
AI.method: The paper introduces a computational interface that translates stochastic unit commitment problems into move-based maximum-weight independent set (MWIS) formulations, retaining classical feasibility recovery.
AI.result: The method was validated on a 15-day trial with a quantum processor, achieving hardware-generated solutions that match or surpass classical benchmarks for 50-node instances. The approach maintains encoding quality while facing challenges at larger scales.
AI.conclusion: This framework enables practical scaling of quantum solutions for industrial scheduling and serves as a foundational step toward tackling larger optimization problems where classical methods may struggle.

title: Higgsino Above the Sea of Fog
summary: Higgsino dark matter is a classic, but still viable, weakly-interacting massive particle (WIMP) scenario that could point to supersymmetry, a new spacetime symmetry of nature. It is a simple realization of the "inelastic dark matter" mechanism, where its scattering off a nucleus occurs between two nearly degenerate states. Intriguingly, very recently the LZ collaboration reported a single nuclear recoil event at a high recoil energy. Assuming that this event is a dark matter candidate, it could be explained by higgsino dark matter, e.g., a 1.1 TeV thermal higgsino with a mass splitting of about 350 keV (using the standard halo model; a much better understanding of the high speed tail in the dark matter velocity distribution is needed for a more precise determination). We map out the parameter space in the higgsino mass and splitting plane that could account for this single LZ event. The needed mass splitting implies that the electroweak gauginos and heavy Higgs scalars in supersymmetry have to be at a much higher scale $\sim (10^3\text{ to }10^4)$ TeV. We discuss possible UV completions to generate a SUSY spectrum in which all superpartners are at a common scale, except for a much lighter higgsino mass $μ$. Besides the thermal benchmark, we comment on possible non-thermal cosmological scenarios of higgsino dark matter with gravitino and modulus decays. The higgsino dark matter scenario could also be searched for at other complementary probes such as indirect detection and future colliders. One striking LZ event may herald an exciting future of further experimental developments.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the implications of a recent LZ collaboration nuclear recoil event, proposing that it could indicate the existence of higgsino dark matter, suggesting supersymmetry and a specific parameter space for its properties.
AI.motivation: The study investigates a potential dark matter signal that may link experimental findings to theoretical frameworks involving supersymmetry and inelastic dark matter mechanisms.
AI.method: We analyze the parameter space related to higgsino dark matter, particularly focusing on its mass and mass splitting, to understand compatibility with observed data, especially the recent nuclear recoil event.
AI.result: Assuming that the recent LZ event is a dark matter interaction, it aligns with the higgsino dark matter hypothesis, necessitating higher mass scales for other supersymmetric particles and allowing for alternative cosmological scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that higgsino dark matter remains a viable candidate, warranting further experimental investigation in various settings including future collider experiments.

title: DF-SQD: Deterministic Fields for Sampling-Based Quantum Diagonalization
summary: Sampling-based quantum diagonalization method exploits Quantum-centric supercomputing platforms to sample bitstrings for Hamiltonian projection on a quantum computer, and then classically diagonalize the Hamiltonian to estimate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. In current quantum devices an algorithm is useful when shallow quantum circuits with error mitigation support can discover better results while having either a proof of convergence or some method to explain trust in experiment. In this paper, we introduce DF-SQD, a hybrid algorithm that derives deterministic auxiliary-field circuits from selected double-factorization leaves of the two-electron tensor. The circuits propose occupation-number configurations, while selected configuration interaction evaluates the original active-space Hamiltonian and can recentre subsequent proposal rounds. On N2 (32 qubits; 6-31G basis) and a 40-qubit [Fe2S2(SCH3)4]2- active-space Hamiltonian, we show that DF-SQD improves the energy obtained from sampled determinant spaces while using shallow number-preserving circuits in both simulator and hardware runs. For N2, DF-SQD is 45x more accurate with a 11.23\% smaller subspace, and due to its ability to sample better bitstrings at lesser shots it is 2.93x faster than SQD in quantum devices. For the iron-sulfur cluster, DF-SQD generated a subspace dimension of 221M with 400K shots, while SQD needed 1.5M shots to generate a 238M subspace, thus we have better subspace recovery evident from the hardware at 3.75x reduced shots. At a matched 50M subspace dimension, DF-SQD is 1.32x more accurate (achieves a 24.5\% relative error reduction over standard SQD). So overall, our method is able to discover better results with shallower circuits, is sample efficient, uses configuration recovery (so has targeted error mitigation) and we have empirical convergence observation.

AI.tldr: The paper presents DF-SQD, a hybrid quantum algorithm that improves eigenvalue estimation by utilizing shallow circuits and enhanced sampling efficiency in quantum computing, yielding better accuracy and smaller subspaces compared to standard methods.
AI.motivation: To enhance quantum eigenvalue estimation and subspace recovery using shallow circuits and error mitigation in quantum devices, addressing limitations of current sampling methods.
AI.method: DF-SQD derives deterministic circuits from double-factorization leaves and employs configuration interaction to evaluate Hamiltonians, sampling bitstrings efficiently.
AI.result: DF-SQD achieves a 45x improvement in accuracy and is 2.93x faster than SQD while using fewer shots, with evidence of better subspace recovery and reduced error.
AI.conclusion: DF-SQD demonstrates significant advancements in quantum sampling efficiency, accuracy, and convergence using shallow number-preserving circuits.

title: Higgsino Dark Matter Interpretation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Nuclear-Recoil Event
summary: We propose Higgsino dark matter as a potential interpretation of the $248~\mathrm{keV}$ nuclear-recoil event of interest reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment. LZ studied several rare background processes and detector effects in detail, but did not identify any as a likely explanation of the event. A nearly pure Higgsino with mass $m_{\widetilde H}\sim1~\mathrm{TeV}$ naturally realizes inelastic dark matter through the off-diagonal $Z$ coupling of two nearly degenerate neutral Majorana states separated by a mass splitting $δ$. The same electroweak interaction fixes the inelastic Higgsino-nucleon scattering cross section, rather than leaving it as a free parameter. We show that the predicted Higgsino inelastic scattering cross section approaches the published LZ two-sided 90% confidence interval for $δ\sim350~\mathrm{keV}$.

AI.tldr: Higgsino dark matter is proposed to explain a specific nuclear-recoil event observed by the LZ experiment, characterized by its unique properties and predicted scattering cross section.
AI.motivation: To provide a viable explanation for the $248~	ext{keV}$ nuclear-recoil event in LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiments, which remains unexplained by known background processes.
AI.method: The paper examines the characteristics of Higgsino dark matter, particularly its inelastic interactions through off-diagonal $Z$ couplings of nearly degenerate Majorana states with a mass splitting $δ$.
AI.result: The study demonstrates that the inelastic Higgsino-nucleon scattering cross section aligns with the LZ experiment's 90% confidence interval for $δ aisebox{0.5ex}{	exttildelow} 350~	ext{keV}$.
AI.conclusion: Higgsino dark matter is a compelling candidate for explaining the observed nuclear-recoil event, with its inelastic scattering properties closely matching experimental data.

title: A nonabelian anyon violates Haag duality
summary: We show that a superselction sector describing a single nonabelian anyon violates Haag duality, which is equivalent to the fundamental quantum-information theoretic principle of uniqueness of purifications. We provide a simple physics argument as well as a rigorous proof using sector theory, and instantiate our result concretely in Levin-Wen models. We also show that the associated ground state does not allow for quantum steering despite being a pure state. Finally, we show that this ground state violates approximate Haag duality, disproving the conjecture that all gapped ground states satisfy this condition. Our result implies that there are gapped phases of matter where Haag duality fails at every point in the phase.

AI.tldr: Nonabelian anyons can violate Haag duality, affecting quantum state purifications.
AI.motivation: To explore the implications of Haag duality violations in the context of nonabelian anyons and gapped phases of matter.
AI.method: The study employs physics arguments and rigorous proofs using sector theory, focusing on Levin-Wen models.
AI.result: Discovered ground states that do not permit quantum steering and show violations of both Haag duality and approximate Haag duality in nonabelian anyon systems.
AI.conclusion: There exist gapped phases of matter that consistently fail to exhibit Haag duality across the entire phase.

title: TeV Higgsino Dark Matter from LZ Nuclear Recoil to Fermi-LAT Gamma Rays
summary: The Higgsino dark matter of the minimal supersymmetric standard model is one of the most minimal and canonical WIMP candidates. We demonstrate that this classic candidate can account for both the high-energy nuclear-recoil excess reported by the LZ experiment and the mild preference in the 14 years of FermiLAT Galactic-center data, with the relic abundance fixing the Higgsino dark matter mass near 1.1 TeV and the recoil spectrum selecting a mass splitting of a few hundred keV. Together with the 10-year IceCube solar-neutrino constraint, the Higgsino interpretation further pins down a viable region of parameter space. It predicts a Galactic-center gamma-ray line and endpoint signal near the present H.E.S.S. sensitivity and within CTAO's projected reach, making this classic candidate testable in the near future.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that Higgsino dark matter can explain recent experimental anomalies and provides specific mass predictions that are testable in future experiments.
AI.motivation: To explore the viability of Higgsino dark matter as a WIMP candidate in light of recent experimental observations.
AI.method: Analyzed high-energy nuclear recoil excess from the LZ experiment, Galactic-center data from FermiLAT, and IceCube solar-neutrino constraints to identify parameter space for Higgsino dark matter.
AI.result: Found that Higgsino dark matter can explain the nuclear-recoil excess and Galactic-center data, fixing its mass near 1.1 TeV and indicating a mass splitting of a few hundred keV.
AI.conclusion: Higgsino dark matter is predicted to produce observable gamma-ray signals, making it a candidate for future tests in gamma-ray observatories like H.E.S.S. and CTAO.

title: Dynamical regimes of QAOA gradient response
summary:
Characterizing the trainability of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) requires understanding how its gradient landscape changes across circuit parameters and problem size. Yet these gradients are usually described in terms of the native QAOA angles, making it difficult to distinguish parameter specific features from broader changes in the underlying circuit dynamics. Here we introduce a dynamical representation of the QAOA parameter space based on a norm-weighted layer strength and a cost--mixer imbalance, separating the overall scale of the evolution from the relative contribution of the two generators.
  Using exact-state simulations of MaxCut, we find that the gradient landscape exhibits a coarse organization in these dynamical variables that persists across changes in circuit depth and schedule structure, while the finer interference pattern remains schedule dependent. Near-optimal solutions do not simply coincide with the largest local gradients, but instead occupy a distinct intermediate dynamical regime. Uniform schedules recover the broad location of this regime, whereas nonuniform schedules mainly reorganize its fine structure. Across the system sizes studied, near-optimal solution regions remain extended in the dynamical representation while their preimages in the native QAOA angles become substantially compressed at larger sizes. These results separate the persistence of useful QAOA dynamics from their accessibility in the native parameterization, and provide a dynamical framework for interpreting QAOA trainability across circuit and problem scales.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a dynamical framework to analyze the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), focusing on the gradient landscape's dependence on circuit parameters and problem size.
AI.motivation: Understanding how the QAOA's gradient landscape evolves helps to distinguish between parameter-specific features and broader circuit dynamics.
AI.method: The authors propose a dynamical representation based on norm-weighted layer strength and cost--mixer imbalance to analyze the QAOA parameter space.
AI.result: The study finds that the gradient landscape organizes itself in a way that remains consistent across varying circuit depth and schedule structures, identifying that near-optimal solutions exist in a distinct dynamical regime.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight the difference between useful QAOA dynamics and their accessibility in native parameters, paving the way for better understanding QAOA trainability across various circuit configurations.

title: A Scalable Multi-Protocol Platform for Quantum Key Distribution Simulation with Rigorous Statistical Evaluation
summary: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) offers information- theoretically secure key establishment grounded in the laws of quantum physics, yet its practical reach is limited by the prohibitive cost of photonic hardware and the fragmented nature of existing simulation tools. Most simulators support only a single protocol and report results from individual stochastic runs, making systematic protocol comparison and reproducible statistical inference difficult. This paper presents a unified QKD simulation platform that implements four foundational protocols BB84, B92, E91, and BBM92 within a single Python/Qiskit engine. A shared impairment model covers fiber attenuation, source and detector losses, po- larization drift, and configurable intercept-resend eavesdropping. The platform is accessible through two independent interfaces that share the same backend: a desktop application (Tkinter, Matplotlib) for local experimentation and a browser-based web client (React, Node.js/Express) for zero-install remote access. All reported results are drawn from repeated-run studies (20 independent runs, 10000 qubits each), with mean, standard deviation, and 95% confidence intervals stated throughout. At a 25 km fiber link, BB84 achieves the highest mean key-rate of 160,045 Hz, followed by BBM92 (80023 Hz), E91 (52815 Hz), and B92 (40011 Hz) ordering that tracks simulation-derived sifting efficiencies precisely. Under the E91 protocol, the CHSH S-statistic averages 2.12 at baseline and falls to 1.58 when an eavesdropper is activated, demonstrating Bell-inequality-based intrusion detection independent of QBER

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified QKD simulation platform that incorporates four foundational protocols (BB84, B92, E91, BBM92) and addresses practicality issues in simulation tools through a comprehensive framework, enhancing systematic comparisons and statistical inference.
AI.motivation: The limitations of existing QKD simulation tools, which typically support only one protocol and hinder reproducible statistical analysis, necessitated the development of a more integrated simulation platform.
AI.method: The study introduces a Python/Qiskit engine that implements four QKD protocols with a unified impairment model, allowing for robust simulations and statistical analysis via both desktop and web interfaces.
AI.result: In simulations, the BB84 protocol demonstrated the highest mean key-rate at 160,045 Hz over a 25 km fiber link, while the E91 protocol provided insights into Bell-inequality-based intrusion detection with varying CHSH S-statistics depending on eavesdropping conditions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed platform enables comprehensive simulation of multiple QKD protocols, fostering better comparisons and insights into protocol performance and security, and demonstrates potential for broader accessibility and application.

title: Decisive evidence for a global cosmic-ray feature in gamma-ray data
summary: We analyze 17 years of Fermi-LAT data to study the diffuse $γ$-ray emission along the Galactic plane and its connection to cosmic-ray (CR) propagation. Accounting for correlated instrumental systematics, we find decisive evidence for a spectral break at $\sim20-30$ GeV, present across the inner Galactic disk, with a preference of $Δχ^2=39.78$ ($4.44 σ$ global). The energy and amplitude of this feature are in striking agreement with the spectral feature observed in local CR nuclei, indicating that it is a global property of the Galactic disk rather than a local phenomenon. The measured slope change, $Δγ\simeq 0.20$, is consistent with local CR data and with expectations from a transition in the CR diffusion regime from Kolmogorov to Kraichnan turbulence. Our results provide strong evidence that diffuse $γ$-ray emission along the Galactic disk is dominated by $π^0-$decay emission up to a hundred GeV. These findings provide key insights into the origin of the CR spectral hardening and the propagation of CRs throughout the Galaxy, and illustrate how this multimessenger approach can be used to probe the origin of features in the CR spectra, such as the long-studied CR Knee.

AI.tldr: The study examines 17 years of Fermi-LAT data to uncover a spectral break in diffuse gamma-ray emission along the Galactic plane, correlating it with cosmic-ray propagation and suggesting it attributes to a broader Galactic phenomenon.
AI.motivation: To understand the connection between diffuse gamma-ray emission and cosmic-ray propagation in the Galactic disk.
AI.method: Analysis of 17 years of Fermi-LAT data, accounting for instrumental systematics, to identify spectral features in gamma-ray emissions.
AI.result: Evidence of a spectral break at 20-30 GeV with a change in slope consistent with local cosmic-ray data, suggesting a transition in cosmic-ray diffusion regimes.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that diffuse gamma-ray emission is dominated by neutral pion decay up to a hundred GeV, offering insights into cosmic-ray spectral hardening and the overall propagation mechanisms in the Galaxy.

title: Emerging Personas and Tools for Hybrid Quantum-HPC Systems
summary: Quantum computing is entering an era where quantum processing units (QPUs) with tens to hundreds of qubits are increasingly integrated with high-performance computing (HPC) systems to support hybrid quantum-classical workloads. This paradigm, often referred to as Quantum-Centric SuperComputing (QCSC), introduces new operational, software, and infrastructure challenges. In this paper, we identify and characterize six distinct personas involved in QCSC environments. Particular attention is given to emerging roles that arise at the interface between quantum and HPC systems. We analyze the responsibilities and tools associated with each persona and examine their differing requirements for operational data. Consistent data representations and analytics frameworks will be required to support diverse users across the quantum-HPC ecosystem. By defining personas and their data needs, we provide a foundation for future discussions in this critical area.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the integration of quantum processing units with high-performance computing, identifying six personas within this hybrid environment, highlighting their roles, responsibilities, and data needs.
AI.motivation: As quantum computing matures and integrates with HPC, distinct user roles are emerging that necessitate understanding their unique challenges and requirements.
AI.method: The paper identifies and characterizes six personas involved in Quantum-Centric SuperComputing (QCSC), analyzing their responsibilities, tools, and operational data needs.
AI.result: The analysis reveals the distinct requirements of varying personas in QCSC environments, emphasizing the need for consistent data representations and analytics frameworks to support diverse users.
AI.conclusion: By defining these personas and their data requirements, the paper establishes a foundation for addressing operational challenges in the quantum-HPC ecosystem.

title: Completing or Refusing Low-Dimensional Records of Structured Quantum Circuits: Measurement Loss, Compression Loss, and Hardware Drift
summary:
Structured quantum circuits are often summarized by low-dimensional records. Records lose control-dependent information when they merge outcomes whose probabilities respond differently to circuit parameters. We assess this loss without a parametric hardware-noise model or low-dimensional statistical family. Quantum Fisher information bounds premeasurement sensitivity; Fisher metrics of measurements and records describe device-attainable sensitivity. A Hellinger residual measures the response removed by a record, while its local quadratic term is the conditional covariance of the full-outcome score. Simultaneous confidence bounds support approval, refusal, or deferral.
  We prove a finite-library completion theorem: executable augmentations terminate with either a record preserving every declared response or proof that no library augmentation removes the loss. For an analytic control germ, integral closures characterize preservation along every analytic control arc, and finitely many Rees valuations detect failure. This state--measurement--record chain connects an all-arc criterion to executable completion or refusal, an attainable-Fisher local kernel criterion, and finite-sample decisions.
  A three-qubit calculation separates measurement loss from record loss. IBM experiments on Kingston and Marrakesh test decisions in fixed-particle-number and GHZ families, including negative controls. An end-to-end Kingston experiment reduces calibration shots by 33.3% while meeting prespecified noninferiority criteria on two held-out objectives. In two-epoch IQM Garnet data, median record-level drift is 0.0797 times full-distribution drift, but a significant residual remains in 35 of 36 settings. These experiments validate failure detection on the tested circuits; they do not establish universal compression performance or device quantum Fisher information.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the loss of control-dependent information in structured quantum circuits due to low-dimensional summaries. It introduces methods to quantify sensitivity and validate findings through experiments on IBM circuits, demonstrating enhanced calibration efficiency while identifying measurement losses.
AI.motivation: To understand how low-dimensional records in quantum circuits lose critical information about circuit parameters and their performance.
AI.method: Utilizes quantum Fisher information to assess sensitivity and employs a novel Hellinger residual for measuring response loss. Introduces a finite-library completion theorem for preserving outcomes in the presence of record loss, validated through theoretical analysis and experimental results on three-qubit circuits.
AI.result: Experiments reveal that while some measurement loss is identified, the methods can reduce calibration attempts by a third while maintaining accuracy, although significant residual losses persist in certain settings.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methods effectively detect failures in quantum circuits and enhance operational efficiency; however, they do not confirm broad applicability for compression performance or establish complete device quantum Fisher information.

title: Fast Microwave-free State Preparation and Measurement of Superconducting Qubits
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, to be submitted to Science Magazine, authors listed alphabetically
summary: Fast, high-fidelity, scalable state preparation and measurement is critical to the realization of a quantum computing system. The state-of-the-art methods for preparation and readout of superconducting qubits require finely tuned microwave signals and ~100 ns of measurement time, which are major obstacles to the scalability and performance of superconducting quantum computers. Here, we have demonstrated novel, microwave-free methods for both preparation and readout of superconducting qubits with >99% fidelity in only 10 ns for either operation while maintaining qubit coherence. This technology is compatible with scalable superconducting digital control systems, and using quantum flux parametrons for amplification, we demonstrated full quantum-to-digital conversion in only 15 ns, which is an order of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art microwave-based techniques.

AI.tldr: Novel microwave-free methods for qubit state preparation and readout achieve >99% fidelity in 10 ns, significantly enhancing scalability for superconducting quantum computers.
AI.motivation: To address scalability and performance limitations caused by traditional microwave techniques in superconducting qubit systems.
AI.method: Developed microwave-free techniques for qubit state preparation and measurement, achieving high fidelity in reduced timeframes.
AI.result: Achieved qubit preparation and readout in 10 ns with >99% fidelity, along with a rapid quantum-to-digital conversion at 15 ns.
AI.conclusion: This advancement offers a promising route for scalable superconducting quantum computing systems.

title: Quantum phase transitions of the Cavity Heisenberg spin-chain
summary: The interplay between quantum criticality and ergodicity breaking constitutes a central challenge in complex quantum many-body systems. Here, we investigate ground-state quantum phase transitions (QPTs) and excited-state quantum phase transitions (ESQPTs), as well as ergodic-nonergodic transition in the cavity Heisenberg spin-chain (CHS) model. By combining quantum information measures with semiclassical fixed-point analysis, we identify a deformed phase that interpolates between the normal and superradiant phases, featuring a logarithmic nonanalyticity in the density of states (DoS) and two additional jump discontinuities. We further elucidate the spectral-structure mechanism underlying the connection between ESQPTs and the ergodic--nonergodic transition (ENET) via level statistics, participation ratios, and multifractal analysis. Our results provide a general framework for characterizing phase structures and spectral features in light--matter quantum many-body systems.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates ground-state and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a cavity Heisenberg spin-chain model, focusing on the interplay of quantum criticality and ergodicity. It identifies a deformed phase and discusses spectral features and their implications for quantum many-body systems.
AI.motivation: The study addresses the complex interplay between quantum criticality and ergodicity breaking in quantum many-body systems, which poses significant challenges in understanding their collective behaviors.
AI.method: The authors employ quantum information measures and semiclassical fixed-point analysis to explore phase transitions and ergodic-nonergodic transitions in the cavity Heisenberg spin-chain model.
AI.result: They identify a deformed phase with unique characteristics, including a logarithmic nonanalyticity in the density of states and additional discontinuities, and elucidate the underlying spectral structure connecting ESQPTs and ENET.
AI.conclusion: The findings contribute a framework for understanding the phase structures and spectral features of light-matter quantum many-body systems.

title: Local Gaussian bounds on the non-destructive discrimination of two-mode squeezed states
summary: Typical measurement setups in quantum systems are destructive, meaning that states are irretrievably altered after measurement. In this work, we analyse non-destructive discrimination of two two-mode squeezed vacuum states using local Gaussian measurements. We investigate a tradeoff relation between the success probability of discrimination and the fidelity of the resulting state with the initial state, and construct a protocol given by local Gaussian measurements, which is optimal within our numerically explored class. We also extend to the case where we allow for additional pre-shared entanglement, and show that this regime allows us to exceed the standard local Gaussian bound for the fidelity-success probability tradeoff. Our work provides a natural extension of the tradeoff between information gain and disturbance in entangled-state discrimination, previously established for finite-dimensional quantum systems, to infinite-dimensional continuous-variable systems.

AI.tldr: This paper explores non-destructive measurement of two-mode squeezed vacuum states in quantum systems using local Gaussian measurements, revealing a tradeoff between success probability and fidelity, and extending previous findings on entangled-state discrimination to continuous-variable systems.
AI.motivation: The research addresses the challenge of destructive measurements in quantum systems by exploring non-destructive measurement techniques for better state preservation.
AI.method: Local Gaussian measurements are employed to discriminate between two two-mode squeezed vacuum states, with a focus on constructing an optimal protocol and analyzing a tradeoff relationship between success probability and fidelity.
AI.result: The study finds that additional pre-shared entanglement allows exceeding the standard local Gaussian limits for fidelity and success probability, establishing a framework for non-destructive discrimination in infinite dimensions.
AI.conclusion: This work generalizes the insights from finite-dimensional quantum systems regarding the information gain-disturbance tradeoff to more complex infinite-dimensional continuous-variable cases.

title: Exact Virtual Channel Programming with Vanishing Excess Overhead
summary: A finite-dimensional physical processor cannot exactly program a continuous family of distinct unitary channels. We show that this obstruction becomes quantitative when the target channel is stored in a normalized Choi state and its output observables are reconstructed by sampling physical channels and classically post-processing their measurement outcomes. For arbitrary $d$-dimensional channels, we construct a target-independent exact reconstruction protocol and prove the optimal one-copy sampling overhead, which grows quadratically with system dimension. We further prove the sharp fixed-$d$ law that the excess overhead vanishes inversely with the number of identical Choi programs. The upper bound combines deterministic port-based teleportation with a quasi-decomposition that corrects its depolarizing distortion. The converse maps any low-overhead reconstruction protocol to a physical learner of unknown unitaries and uses local quantum estimation to recover the same leading coefficient. These results recast the universal no-programming obstruction as a quantitative trade-off between quantum program memory and classical sampling, with a leading cost that reflects the locally learnable unitary degrees of freedom.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies the limitations of finite-dimensional processors in programming continuous unitary channels, introducing a reconstruction protocol that addresses sampling overhead and its dependence on system dimensions.
AI.motivation: To understand the limitations of programming continuous unitary channels in finite-dimensional physical systems and provide a reconstruction method for such channels.
AI.method: The authors construct a target-independent exact reconstruction protocol and establish the sampling overhead's behavior as a function of the system's dimension, utilizing techniques like deterministic port-based teleportation and local quantum estimation.
AI.result: The study demonstrates that the optimal one-copy sampling overhead scales quadratically with the dimension of the system, while showing that excess overhead decreases inversely with the number of identical programs used.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight a fundamental trade-off between the memory required for quantum programming and the classical sampling needed for accurate channel reconstruction.

title: Verifiable quantum advantage in extremely low depth
summary: We give a sampling problem that is solvable by shallow quantum circuits, hard for polynomial-time classical algorithms under lattice-based assumptions, and efficiently verifiable by a classical computer. The quantum sampler admits two implementations: one uses log-logarithmic-depth quantum circuits with one- and two-qubit gates, i.e., $\mathsf{QNC}^0[\log\log]$ circuits, while the other uses constant-depth quantum circuits with unbounded fan-in gates, i.e., $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits. Our construction can be seen as compiling the Learning with Errors (LWE)-based single-round proof of quantumness of Arabadjieva et al. (2025) to very low depth. The price paid for this compilation is the reliance on less standard, though well-motivated, assumptions: in addition to the lattice knowledge assumption used by Arabadjieva et al. (2025), we require a strengthened variant of the adaptive-hardcore-bit property of LWE, for which we provide supporting evidence. Unlike previous low-depth proofs of quantumness, the quantum computation here requires no mid-circuit measurements or feed-forward: it consists only of running a shallow circuit and sampling from its output distribution. This shows that shallow quantum circuits have sufficient structure to solve certain classically hard tasks whose solutions can be verified efficiently.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a sampling problem solvable by shallow quantum circuits, hard for classical algorithms under lattice assumptions, and verifiable classically, showcasing efficient quantum implementations and their structural benefits.
AI.motivation: To explore the capabilities of shallow quantum circuits in solving classically hard problems, while highlighting their verifiability and efficiency.
AI.method: Two implementations of a quantum sampler: one with log-logarithmic-depth circuits using one- and two-qubit gates ($	ext{QNC}^0[	ext{log log}]$) and another with constant-depth circuits using unbounded fan-in gates ($	ext{QAC}^0$).
AI.result: A sampling problem demonstrating efficiency in shallow quantum circuits with no mid-circuit measurements, solving classically hard tasks while requiring specific lattice-based assumptions.
AI.conclusion: Shallow quantum circuits can tackle certain hard problems efficiently, revealing the underlying structure necessary for quantum computation without complex measurement overhead.

title: Quantum Weighted Moving Average for Predicting Limit Order Book Trends
summary: Can quantum computers be useful for forecasting multivariate financial time series? In this work, we consider the problem of predicting price trends from limit order book (LOB) data. After identifying key components of classical models, we introduce the quantum weighted moving average (QWMA) model. The two main building blocks are, first, classically preprocessing via normalization of both feature and temporal dimensions and, second, a linear combination of unitaries-based layer for unitarily-embedded classical data. The models are evaluated on the FI-2010 benchmark dataset and a second dataset of China A-share stocks. While we do not present evidence of quantum advantage, the combined classical-quantum model demonstrates performances close to the best classical models. The quantum part of the model is expressive enough to focus on the most predictive parts of the time series. Several specializations of the QWMA model are considered, in particular a variant related to the widely-used exponential moving average (EMA). We give consideration to the limitations of the methods and the datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the potential of quantum computing in forecasting financial time series using a novel quantum weighted moving average (QWMA) model, showing close performance to classical approaches despite not achieving quantum advantage.
AI.motivation: To assess the feasibility of quantum computers in predicting multivariate financial time series, particularly using limit order book data.
AI.method: Introduction of the QWMA model, involving classical preprocessing and a quantum layer for data analysis, evaluated on benchmark datasets including FI-2010 and China A-shares.
AI.result: The combined classical-quantum model performs comparably to top classical models without demonstrating quantum advantage, while effectively focusing on predictive aspects of the time series.
AI.conclusion: The QWMA model shows potential in financial predictions, although limitations exist in the current methodologies and datasets.

title: Irreducibility and regularisation properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
comment: 32 pages, comments and remarks are welcome
summary:
We study regularisation and irreducibility properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups (GQMSs) acting on continuous-variable quantum systems. We first identify a natural notion of regularity for operators in this setting, which allows us to formulate and characterise the smoothing effects of GQMSs in terms of algebraic conditions involving the drift and quantum diffusion matrices. These conditions establish a connection with the controllability theory of quantum linear systems and with the structure of decoherence-free subsystems.
  We then characterise irreducibility through several equivalent algebraic criteria: one formulated in terms of the drift and quantum diffusion matrices, one in terms of the operators appearing in the generalised GKLS representation of the generator, and a third given by a quantum analogue of Hörmander's condition. A central and somewhat surprising consequence is that, in contrast with the classical case, irreducibility is strictly stronger than conditions ensuring regularisation. Our results provide an algebraic framework for analysing these properties and lay the groundwork for a broader study of reducible Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups and, more generally, more general relevant quantum Markov semigroups on continuous-variable systems.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the regularization and irreducibility of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups, offering algebraic criteria and revealing that irreducibility is a stronger condition than regularization, thereby advancing the understanding of these quantum systems.
AI.motivation: To understand the regularization and irreducibility properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups acting on continuous-variable quantum systems, enhancing their analysis.
AI.method: The study involves identifying notions of regularity and establishing algebraic conditions related to drift and quantum diffusion matrices, alongside characterizing irreducibility through multiple algebraic criteria.
AI.result: The findings indicate that irreducibility is stronger than conditions for regularization, highlighting a distinct difference from classical systems and providing a mathematical framework for further research.
AI.conclusion: This research lays the groundwork for a deeper investigation into reducible Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups and related quantum systems, aiding in the understanding of their dynamic properties.

title: Depth-1 expanders on the unitary group and applications
summary:
We construct a constant-degree and constant-gap quantum expander on $n$ qubits where each unitary can be implemented by a depth-$1$ and 1D circuit of Pauli or CNOT gates. We provide two applications of this expander. First, we use it to construct a family of frustration-free 1D Hamiltonians whose ground states obey the entanglement-gap relation $S = Θ(Δ^{-1/2})$; this is believed to be optimal, but achieving it had been open. Second, we use it to provide a streaming protocol that tests for closeness to a class of 1D volume-law entangled states.
  Moreover, we extend our quantum expander to a constant-degree and constant-gap expander on the unitary group where each unitary is a single $T$ gate, a single $T^{\dagger}$ gate, or a depth-$1$ Clifford circuit. This implies that a random sequence of unitaries from the expander yields a gapped walk on a dense subgroup of the unitary group. This improves upon previous work by Bourgain and Gamburd which did not control the dependence of the gap on the dimension.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a constant-degree quantum expander constructed on n qubits via depth-1, 1D circuits of Pauli or CNOT gates, with applications in frustration-free Hamiltonians and streaming protocols for 1D entangled states.
AI.motivation: The goal is to construct quantum expanders that can lead to significant advancements in quantum information theory, specifically regarding the entanglement-gap relation and testing volume-law entangled states.
AI.method: The authors develop a quantum expander using constant-degree and constant-gap structures that leverage depth-1 circuits with specific gates, extending this to a unitary group expander involving T and Cliffords to achieve gapped walks.
AI.result: The constructed expander allows for the realization of frustration-free Hamiltonians with optimal entanglement-gap relations and supports a streaming protocol for testing 1D entangled states, while controlling the dimension-related gap.

title: Observable- and state-selective prethermalization and bounds on prethermal lifetimes
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures; This manuscript presents the dynamical part of the work originally posted on arXiv as [arXiv.2607.15350v1], which has since been split into two papers. That arXiv manuscript now contains only the static part
summary: Prethermalization describes long-lived intermediate regimes that precede equilibrium and can dominate experimentally accessible dynamics. Here, we show that a separation of spectral energy scales, despite giving rise to a hierarchy of dynamical timescales, does not by itself guarantee the appearance of a prethermal plateau. Under the same Hamiltonian, some observables may exhibit prethermal behavior, while others relax directly toward equilibrium. We uncover the mechanism governing this selectivity, showing that the emergence of a prethermal plateau depends not only on the Hamiltonian, but also on the observable and the initial state. Our results apply broadly to systems close to a fully permutation-symmetric limit and are illustrated with a long-range interacting spin model. We further prove that the Loschmidt echo provides a lower bound on the prethermal lifetime of any bounded observable whenever the prethermal and exact dynamics are unitary.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates prethermalization, revealing that the emergence of a prethermal plateau depends on the observable, initial state, and Hamiltonian, despite having distinct timescales.
AI.motivation: To understand the conditions under which prethermalization occurs in dynamic systems and its implications on observables.
AI.method: Analysis of spectral energy scales and their influence on the dynamics of observables in a long-range interacting spin model, along with proving a lower bound on the prethermal lifetime using the Loschmidt echo.
AI.result: Demonstrates that not all observables exhibit prethermal behavior under the same Hamiltonian; some relax directly to equilibrium depending on initial conditions and observables.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight the complexity of prethermalization, indicating its selective nature influenced by various factors, thus providing deeper insights into non-equilibrium dynamics.
